And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these
that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? –Luke 24:17.

On June 6, 1944, 156,000 American, British, and Canadian troops landed on a 50-mile stretch of beach in Normandy, France. After several months of intense fighting, they overcame the initial defenses and swarmed into the German-held territory. The surprise attack, known as D-Day, caught the Germans off guard. However, it wasn’t until March of the next year that France was finally liberated from German forces. D-day was the beginning of the end of World War II on the western front and it was the event that seemed to sap the life from the notorious German army, from which they never recovered. It appears rather coincidental that so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.

I can imagine that these two believers, plodding upon the road to Emmaus that dim and dismal evening, were feeling a little the same way. Their D-Day had arrived totally unexpected. I would suspect that every living person has at one time or another experienced moments of intense sadness—their own D-day, so-to-speak. Even some animals have been known to express a melancholy mood at the death of their master or mate. But these two disciples seemed to be experiencing a pain far beyond the normal loss of a friend. They were staring into the face of the grim reality that all their bright hopes of a shining tomorrow were hopelessly shattered in a ruinous heap at the foot of the cross.

This agony was no ordinary fit of depression but rather it was a depression linked to a crisis of faith. This type of discouragement is a state of intense spiritual anguish in which the struggling, despairing believer feels he is abandoned by God. It is a hopeless feeling that the sun of God's blessedness has been eclipsed and the dark night of the soul has become a permanent resident within.

While all of us seek to valiantly resist such dark temptations, a brief search into the lives of many godly men will reveal that these temptations are very real and are quite common to man. In such a condition, life seems impossible and the impending gloom that has settled upon the heart sees no light at the end of the tunnel. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed? wilt thou be altogether unto me as a liar, and as waters that fail? –Jeremiah 15:18. This is obviously an overstated exaggeration that escaped the lips of the weeping prophet, but it gives us a direct snapshot into the dreaded pain in the depths of his soul.

For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:8-9. This dark night of the soul shows no respect to persons. It invades the lives of princes and paupers, preachers and penitents, public and private people, pulpits and pews. These two disciples had verbally revisited every possible scenario in their journey along the Emmaus Road. They had no doubt found plenty of fault in others as well as personal regret. The “what ifs” and “if onlys” had thoroughly been discussed, but nothing could reverse the outcome and their restless anxiety lingered still.

The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs or approximately seven miles. And along this doleful journey a Stranger joined ranks with the distraught duo in their D-Day and asked them for an account of their sadness. But he is no curious onlooker. He is the risen Lord who has come to cast His heavenly light upon our darkened pathway. Rather than revealing Himself abruptly, and perhaps for our benefit, he patiently allows them to expose the depleted spiritual road that they were treading upon.

Thus, the conversation unfolds as the mile markers pass, each revealing our sincere erroneous efforts that lead us further from the city of peace and into the dark night of the soul…

…The Ignorance of Others

And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? –Luke 24:18. Ask any stranger on the streets of New York City why the flags were flying at half-mast three days after the towers fell on September 11, and you would receive the same incredulous answer ascribed to these two. “How can you be so ignorant?” We all tend to marvel at people who do not hold the same knowledge that we imagine ourselves to possess. The younger the man, the more answers that he believes the coffers of his understanding hold.

This is nothing new. Moses, as a young man, …supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not –Acts 7:25. While he firmly understood that he owned the plan of God, he was badly mistaken in the percentage that he possessed. If our recourse cannot rectify the given situation, our answers are not the real answer. The heartfelt disdain that naturally arises toward those who see it differently is the beginning marker that we are on the wrong path. Miles down the pathway of life, Moses began to feel the desperation of that pain and the darkness of the hour. I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me. And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness –Numbers 11:14-15. Why did Moses not see this earlier in life? For the same cause that these two fervent disciples’ …eyes were holden that they should not know him –Luke 24:16.

…Reason

And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people –Luke 24:19. They had their private perception of who the Christ was, but they were seeing …through a glass, darkly… –1 Corinthians 13:12. Their partial knowledge was leaning heavily on their own understanding and looking for the wrong kind of redemption. To them, their redeemer was (past tense) a prophet that no longer could do what they wanted him to do. We all want Jesus to solve our problems and make us feel better, but His purpose is to free us from our presumption and sin.

Jacob had every reason to believe that the birthright and blessing was to be his. At Bethel, God had promised to bless him. Jacob reckoned this to arrive in a material format. And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God –Genesis 28:20-21.

But the greatest blessing he ever received from God arrived to him on the wings of a deep dark night. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him. And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed –Genesis 32:24-28.

Jacob had already accumulated an abundance of earthly possessions. What more could he want? It was a dark night for Jacob when he discovered that he’d spent his life pursuing possessions and resisting God. He now seeks godly character and spiritual affluence. His victory was through surrender, and he limped away as a cripple with a crown. The Lord cannot fully bless a man until He has first conquered his powers of reason.

…Ill Fate

And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him –Luke 24:20. God specializes in turning grave dilemmas into monumental victories. Still, man looks around him and curses the darkness about him. Though there may be a volley of good reciprocating them, …the morning is to them even as the shadow of death… –Job 24:17. To give undo emphasis upon the evil about us is to mock the divinity of God. While we all may regret at times things that we could have done or said differently, we must invariably leave the results in the hands of God. Job experienced as much ill fate as anybody. So much so that he opened …his mouth, and cursed his day. And Job spake, and said, Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived. Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it. Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. As for that night, let darkness seize upon it… –Job 3:1-6. But somewhere before the dark events were rectified and lifted, the light shined into his soul, and he laid his hand to his mouth and worshiped.

…Personal Agenda

But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel… –Luke 24:21. It is but natural to attempt to understand any given situation and these two had selected the correct equation. Their folly lay in the presumption of the means that Christ was to perform this and the type of redemption they were to receive. They were looking forward to the day when their nation would be exalted over the Romans. When we unwittingly seek our own security, it is bound to lead to bitter disappointment. Naaman thought …He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper –2 Kings 5:11.

Abraham was promised the land of Canaan and he asked for a confirmation. He then prepared the covenant sacrifice prescribed by God, but the entire day passed, and God did nothing with them. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. –Genesis 15:12.

As Abraham waited on God to receive his offering, he continued to beat back the birds of prey. But as the day neared an end he began to feel abandoned by God and the dark night began to settle upon his soul. It takes a midnight experience for things to get dark enough for us to see the stars and quiet enough to hear His voice. But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:9.

…Impatience

…And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done –Luke 24:21. Many of us are disciplined enough to hold out for a season. It is when our hope is deferred (see Proverbs 13:12) that our hearts grow sick and faint. Three days seemed like a long time to these two. But three days, weeks, months, years, or even decades are all within the disposal of God’s clock. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? –Psalm 13:1.

Joseph patiently endured the ill treatment of his brothers and Potiphar, but the dungeon got long, and he entreated the butler to send for him when he was restored his position. But it was two full years (Genesis 41:1) until Pharoah dreamed and Joseph was finally hailed forth. But it was not so much the fault of the butler as it was the will of God who had called Joseph to be …laid in iron: Until the time that his word came: the word of the LORD tried him –Psalm 105:18-19. There is no more effective avenue to teach us patience than the discipline of darkness, from which few saints are exempt.

…Self-Pity

Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre; And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive –Luke 24:22-23. No one enjoys missing out. In fact, psychology has uncovered a new disorder –FOMO (fear of missing out). The tidings brought by the women was good news and an amazing turn of events, yet it brought the others no joy for it did not happen to them. Good news can rarely penetrate a person immersed in self-pity and Elijah was one such. His dark night arrived on the heels of a breathtaking triumph on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal. But in the blackness of his own inner feelings …he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers –1 Kings 19:4.

…Feelings of Failure

And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not –Luke 24:24. It is easy to think, “It worked for them but it’s not working for me.” While unsuccessful efforts may discourage us, it is not necessarily a failure on our part. John the Baptist had faithfully called the people to repentance, baptized Christ, and witnessed the thundering voice from heaven. He accurately announced the coming Messiah and pointed his disciples to …the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world –John 1:29. This ministry earned him a secure place in a dark prison cell. He had been well accustomed to the lack of comfort and a meager diet, but it was the feelings of utter abandonment by God that brought him unto dark doubts. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? –Luke 7:19.

“Was I wrong?” In the darkness he began to experience life on the sloping back of a question mark. John Bunyan describes it as the slough of despond. It may appear like D-Day for the Christian, but undue emphasis upon our unsuccessful efforts promotes no resurrection.

Conclusion

Not all spiritual darkness is completely avoidable. Not every spiritual experience is a time of heartfelt blessing, nor is every place. There are times of persecution and testing that are designed to bring saints unto the soul reckoning that only dark nights can minister unto. Jesus Himself was tempted in a similar manner to us, when in the pervading darkness of the ninth hour on the cross, His voice rang out …with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? –Matthew 27:46.

The road to Emmaus bears witness to the fact that a vibrant existence of faith gives no guarantee of the absence of spiritual depression. It is a story about real people with real faith experiencing real trials. It is helpful to teach us that even spiritual pleasures ought not to be held too tightly. Our confident visions for the future both immediate and long term must be immersed in the fires of humility. The dark night is the place where such self-deception dies, and an intimate knowledge of God is birthed. It transitions us from loving God for the blessings He gives us, to loving God for our relationship with Him and the communion that follows.

The traveling companion of Cleopas was never mentioned. Some think it was his wife. Some claim it was Luke. But their identity was omitted, perhaps so that we might be more apt to fill the vacancy with our own name. Seven miles from Jerusalem we stumble upon the stark reality of whom the Savior really is and that salvation is more than just a rubber stamp marking His possession. The scales fall from our eyes and the dark night of the soul gives way to the brightness of the noonday light of the presence of God. It is then that we make our joyous dash back to the city of peace only to be misunderstood again. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them –Mark 16:13.

And so, I wonder even at the profitability of writing down such thoughts. It is not an encounter that can be manufactured and intellectually understood. It is a highly personal convocation with God and tailored specifically to each individual. But perhaps we, in our shallow generation, can be encouraged to reach out and embrace the darkness instead of meeting it with a loathing resistance. And there in the menacing darkness of night, learn to embrace the Savior of light.

Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature's night.
Thine eye diffused a quickening ray,
I woke; the dungeon flamed with light.
My chains fell off. My heart was free.
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

- Charles Wesley

Dan Ia berkata kepada mereka, Apakah percakapan yang demikian ini yang kamu ada seorang kepada yang lain,
di waktu kamu berjalan dan sedih? –Lukas 24:17.

Pada 6 Juni 1944, 156.000 pasukan Amerika, Inggris, dan Kanada mendarat di sebuah pantai sepanjang 50 mil di Normandy, Prancis. Setelah beberapa bulan pertempuran sengit, mereka menembus pertahanan awal dan menyerbu ke wilayah yang dikuasai Jerman. Serangan kejutan itu, yang dikenal sebagai D-Day, mengejutkan pihak Jerman. Namun, baru pada Maret tahun berikutnya Prancis akhirnya dibebaskan dari pasukan Jerman. D-Day adalah awal dari akhir Perang Dunia II di front barat dan merupakan peristiwa yang tampaknya menguras kehidupan dari tentara Jerman yang terkenal itu, dari mana mereka tak pernah pulih. Tampak cukup kebetulan bahwa begitu banyak kata-kata dengan konotasi negatif diawali dengan huruf D: Kekecewaan, Keraguan, Duka, Kehancuran, Kepahitan, Kegelapan, Kekalahan, Keputusasaan, Depresi, Musnah, Penghancuran, Penipuan, dan Kematian.

Saya dapat membayangkan bahwa kedua orang percaya ini, berjalan lesu di jalan menuju Emmaus pada malam yang suram itu, merasakan sedikit hal yang sama. D-Day mereka tiba sama sekali tak terduga. Saya curiga bahwa setiap orang yang hidup pada satu waktu atau lainnya pernah mengalami momen-momen kesedihan mendalam—D-day mereka, bisa dikatakan. Bahkan beberapa binatang dikenal menunjukkan suasana melankolis atas kematian tuan atau pasangannya. Tetapi kedua murid ini tampaknya mengalami rasa sakit yang jauh melampaui kehilangan biasa seorang teman. Mereka menatap wajah kenyataan suram bahwa semua harapan cerah mereka akan hari esok yang gemilang hancur tak berdaya menjadi tumpukan reruntuhan di kaki salib.

Kesengsaraan ini bukanlah serangan depresi biasa melainkan depresi yang terkait dengan krisis iman. Jenis keputusasaan ini adalah keadaan kesengsaraan rohani yang intens di mana orang percaya yang bergumul dan putus asa merasa ditinggalkan oleh Tuhan. Itu adalah perasaan tanpa harap bahwa matahari kebahagiaan Tuhan telah tertutup dan malam yang gelap dalam jiwa menjadi penghuni tetap di dalamnya.

Sementara kita semua berusaha dengan gagah berani menolak godaan gelap seperti itu, sedikit menelusuri kehidupan banyak orang saleh akan mengungkapkan bahwa godaan-godaan ini sangat nyata dan cukup umum dialami manusia. Dalam kondisi seperti itu, hidup tampak mustahil dan kegelapan yang menyelimuti hati tidak melihat cahaya di ujung terowongan. Mengapa kesengsaraanku tetap ada, dan patah hatiku tak tersembuhkan, yang tidak mau disembuhkan? Apakah Engkau hendak menjadi kepadaku seperti dusta, dan seperti air yang habis? –Yeremia 15:18. Ini jelas merupakan pernyataan yang melebih-lebihkan yang keluar dari bibir nabi yang menangis, tetapi itu memberi kita cuplikan langsung ke dalam rasa sakit yang ditakuti di dasar jiwanya.

Sebab kami tidak mau, saudara-saudara, supaya kamu tidak mengetahui kesesakan kami yang terjadi atas kami di Asia, bahwa kami ditindas melebihi kekuatan, sehingga kami putus asa bahkan dari hidup: tetapi kami telah menerima hukuman maut dalam diri kami, supaya kami jangan bergantung pada diri sendiri, tetapi pada Allah yang membangkitkan orang mati –2 Korintus 1:8-9. Malam gelap jiwa ini tidak memandang orang. Ia menyerbu kehidupan pangeran dan orang miskin, pengkhotbah dan pendosa yang menyesal, orang-orang umum dan pribadi, mimbar dan bangku. Kedua murid ini secara lisan telah mengulang setiap kemungkinan skenario dalam perjalanan mereka di Jalan Emmaus. Mereka tak diragukan lagi menemukan banyak kesalahan pada orang lain serta penyesalan pribadi. “Bagaimana jika” dan “seandainya” telah dibahas tuntas, tetapi tak ada yang dapat membalikkan hasil dan kegelisahan mereka tetap bertahan.

Jalan dari Yerusalem ke Emmaus adalah sekitar enam puluh stadion atau kira-kira tujuh mil. Dan sepanjang perjalanan yang muram ini seorang Orang Asing bergabung dengan pasangan yang gelisah itu pada D-Day mereka dan menanyakan kepada mereka tentang kesedihan mereka. Tetapi Ia bukan sekadar pengamat penasaran. Ia adalah Tuhan yang bangkit yang datang untuk menyorotkan terang surgawi-Nya pada jalan kita yang gelap. Daripada menyatakan diri-Nya secara mendadak, dan mungkin demi keuntungan mereka, Ia dengan sabar membiarkan mereka membuka jalan rohani yang terkuras yang sedang mereka pijaki.

Demikianlah percakapan itu berkembang saat penanda mil berlalu, masing-masing mengungkapkan upaya keliru kita yang tulus yang membawa kita semakin jauh dari kota damai dan ke dalam malam gelap jiwa…

…Ketidaktahuan Orang Lain

Dan salah seorang dari mereka yang bernama Kleopas menjawab Dia: "Engkahulah orang asing di Yerusalem, dan tidak tahukah Engkau apa yang terjadi di sana pada hari-hari ini?" –Lukas 24:18. Tanyakan pada siapa pun yang asing di jalan-jalan New York mengapa bendera dikibarkan setengah tiang tiga hari setelah menara runtuh pada 11 September, dan Anda akan mendapat jawaban tak percaya yang sama seperti yang dikatakan kedua orang ini. "Bagaimana mungkin engkau begitu tidak tahu?" Kita semua cenderung heran terhadap orang yang tidak memiliki pengetahuan yang sama seperti yang kita bayangkan kita miliki. Semakin muda seseorang, semakin banyak jawaban yang dipercayainya tersimpan dalam peti pemahamannya.

Ini bukan hal baru. Musa, pada waktu muda, …mengira saudara-saudaranya akan menyadari bahwa Allah oleh tangannya akan melepaskan mereka: tetapi mereka tidak mengerti –Kisah Para Rasul 7:25. Sementara ia dengan teguh memahami bahwa ia memegang rencana Allah, ia salah besar dalam persentase yang dimilikinya. Jika upaya kita tidak dapat memperbaiki situasi yang ada, jawaban kita bukanlah jawaban yang sebenarnya. Kebencian yang timbul di hati terhadap mereka yang melihatnya berbeda adalah tanda awal bahwa kita berada di jalan yang salah. Beberapa mil di jalan hidup, Musa mulai merasakan keputusasaan akan rasa sakit itu dan kegelapan saat itu. Aku tidak sanggup memikul bangsa ini seorang diri, karena amat berat bagi aku; jika Engkau memperlakukan aku demikian, maka bunuhlah aku saja, kiranya aku beroleh kasih karunia di mata-Mu, dan janganlah biarkan aku melihat kebinasaan aku –Bilangan 11:14-15. Mengapa Musa tidak melihat ini lebih awal dalam hidupnya? Karena sebab yang sama yang membuat kedua murid yang bersemangat itu …matanya tertutup supaya mereka tidak mengenal Dia –Lukas 24:16.

…Ia Mengandalkan Akal

Dan Ia berkata kepada mereka, Apakah perkara-perkara itu? Jawab mereka: Tentang Yesus orang Nazaret, yang ialah nabi yang kuat dalam perkataan dan perbuatan di hadapan Allah dan segala bangsa –Lukas 24:19. Mereka mempunyai persepsi pribadi tentang siapa Kristus itu, tetapi mereka melihat …seperti dalam cermin, dengan tidak jelas… –1 Korintus 13:12. Pengetahuan sebagian mereka terlalu mengandalkan pengertian sendiri dan mencari jenis penyelamatan yang salah. Bagi mereka, Juruselamat mereka adalah (dalam bentuk lampau) seorang nabi yang tidak lagi dapat melakukan apa yang mereka ingin Ia lakukan. Kita semua ingin Yesus menyelesaikan masalah kita dan membuat kita merasa lebih baik, tetapi tujuan-Nya adalah membebaskan kita dari kesombongan dan dosa kita.

Yakub punya setiap alasan untuk percaya bahwa hak kesulungan dan berkat akan menjadi miliknya. Di Betel, Allah telah berjanji untuk memberkatinya. Yakub membayangkan ini akan tiba dalam bentuk materi. Yakub membuat nazar, katanya: "Jika Allah menyertai aku, dan memeliharaku dalam perjalanan ini yang aku lakukan, dan memberi aku roti makan dan pakaian untuk dipakai, sehingga aku pulang lagi ke rumah bapaku dalam keadaan selamat, maka TUHAN akan menjadi Allahku –Kejadian 28:20-21.

Namun berkat terbesar yang pernah diterimanya dari Allah datang kepadanya melalui malam yang sangat gelap. Dan Yakub tinggal seorang diri; maka bergumullah seorang dengan dia hingga fajar. Ketika ia melihat, bahwa ia tidak dapat mengalahkan dia, ia menimpakan tangan pada lipat pahanya; lalu terpencallah lipat pahanya, ketika ia bergumul dengan dia. Lalu ia berkata: "Biarkanlah aku pergi, sebab fajar sudah menyingsing." Tetapi ia berkata: "Aku tidak akan melepaskan engkau, sebelum engkau memberkatiku." Maka ia bertanya kepadanya: "Apakah namamu?" Jawabnya: "Yakub." Lalu ia berkata: "Nama-mu tidak lagi akan disebut Yakub, melainkan Israel; sebab engkau telah berjuang dengan Allah dan dengan manusia dan engkau menang –Kejadian 32:24-28.

Yakub sudah mengumpulkan banyak harta dunia. Apalagi yang ia mau? Adalah malam gelap bagi Yakub ketika ia mendapati bahwa ia telah menghabiskan hidupnya mengejar kepemilikan dan menentang Allah. Sekarang ia mencari karakter yang saleh dan kekayaan rohani. Kemenangannya adalah melalui penyerahan, dan ia berlumpuh pergi sebagai orang pincang dengan mahkota. Tuhan tidak dapat memberkati sepenuhnya seorang manusia sampai Ia terlebih dahulu menaklukkan kekuatan akalnya.

…Nasib Buruk

Dan bagaimana imam-imam kepala dan penguasa-penguasa kita menyerahkan Dia supaya dihukum mati dan disalibkan-Nya Dia –Lukas 24:20. Allah ahli dalam mengubah dilema berat menjadi kemenangan monumental. Namun, manusia melihat sekelilingnya dan mengutuk kegelapan itu. Meskipun mungkin ada balasan kebaikan yang beruntun, …pagi bagi mereka sama seperti bayang-bayang maut… –Ayub 24:17. Memberi penekanan yang berlebihan pada kejahatan di sekitar kita berarti mencemooh keilahian Allah. Walaupun kita semua kadang menyesali hal-hal yang dapat kita lakukan atau katakan berbeda, kita harus menyerahkan hasilnya kepada Allah. Ayub mengalami nasib buruk sebesar siapa pun. Begitu sampai ia membuka …mulutnya dan mengutuk hari kelahirannya. Ayub berkata: "Hancurlah hari ketika aku dilahirkan, dan malam ketika dikatakan: "telah lahir seorang anak laki-laki." Biarlah hari itu menjadi gelap; biarlah Allah tidak memandang dari atas; biarlah terang tidak bersinar di atasnya. Biarlah kegelapan dan bayang-bayang maut menutupinya; biarlah awan tinggal di atasnya; biarlah kegelapan hari itu menakutinya. Mengenai malam itu, biarlah kegelapan menyergapnya… –Ayub 3:1-6. Tetapi entah bagaimana sebelum peristiwa-peristiwa gelap itu dibetulkan dan diangkat, terang bersinar ke dalam jiwanya, dan ia meletakkan tangannya ke mulutnya dan beribadah.

…Agenda Pribadi

Tetapi kami berharap, bahwa Dialah yang akan menebus Israel… –Lukas 24:21. Adalah wajar mencoba memahami suatu keadaan dan kedua orang ini telah memilih persamaan yang benar. Kesalahan mereka terletak pada anggapan tentang cara yang akan dipakai Kristus untuk melakukannya dan jenis penebusan yang mereka harapkan. Mereka menantikan hari ketika bangsa mereka akan ditinggikan atas orang Romawi. Ketika tanpa sadar kita mencari keamanan sendiri, itu pasti akan membawa kepada kekecewaan pahit. Naaman berpikir …Ia tentu akan datang menghadap aku, berdiri dan berseru kepada nama TUHAN, Allahnya, dan mengulurkan tangan ke tempat itu, dan menyembuhkan kusta itu –2 Raja-raja 5:11.

Abraham dijanjikan tanah Kanaan dan ia meminta tanda pengesahan. Ia lalu menyiapkan korban perjanjian yang ditetapkan Allah, tetapi sepanjang hari berlalu dan Allah tidak melakukan apa-apa dengan mereka. Ketika matahari hendak terbenam, maka tertidurlah Abram; dan tiba-tiba tampaklah kengerian kegelapan yang besar menimpa dia –Kejadian 15:12.

Saat Abraham menunggu Allah menerima persembahannya, ia terus menghalau burung pemangsa. Tetapi ketika hari hampir berakhir ia mulai merasa ditinggalkan oleh Allah dan malam gelap mulai turun ke dalam jiwanya. Diperlukan pengalaman tengah malam agar keadaan menjadi cukup gelap untuk kita melihat bintang-bintang dan cukup tenang untuk mendengar suara-Nya. Tetapi kami telah menerima hukuman maut dalam diri kami, supaya kami jangan bergantung pada diri sendiri, tetapi pada Allah yang membangkitkan orang mati –2 Korintus 1:9.

…Ketidaksabaran

...Dan selain semuanya itu, hari ini adalah hari ketiga sejak hal-hal ini terjadi –Lukas 24:21. Banyak dari kita cukup berdisiplin untuk bertahan untuk suatu musim. Ketika pengharapan kita tertunda (lihat Amsal 13:12) hati kita menjadi sakit dan lemah. Tiga hari tampak lama bagi kedua orang ini. Tetapi tiga hari, minggu, bulan, tahun, atau bahkan dekade semuanya berada dalam kuasa jam Tuhan. Berapa lama lagi Engkau akan melupakan aku, ya TUHAN? sampai selama-lamanya? berapa lama lagi Engkau akan menyembunyikan wajah-Mu dari padaku? –Mazmur 13:1.

Yusuf dengan sabar menanggung perlakuan buruk saudara-saudaranya dan Potifar, tetapi penjara terasa lama, dan ia memohon kepada juru minuman anggur supaya diingatkan kepadanya apabila ia dipulihkan. Namun butuh dua tahun penuh (Kejadian 41:1) sampai Firaun bermimpi dan Yusuf akhirnya dipanggil keluar. Tetapi bukan semata-mata karena kesalahan juru minuman anggur melainkan kehendak Allah yang memanggil Yusuf untuk …ditaruh dalam belenggu: Sampai datang waktunya akan firman-Nya: firman TUHAN menguji dia –Mazmur 105:18-19. Tidak ada jalan yang lebih efektif untuk mengajar kita kesabaran selain disiplin kegelapan, yang hampir tidak ada orang kudus yang luput darinya.

…Kasihan Diri

Ya, ada juga perempuan-perempuan dari kami yang menjadikan kami heran, yang dahulu pergi ke kubur; dan ketika mereka tidak menemukan tubuh-Nya, mereka kembali memberitakan bahwa mereka telah melihat juga suatu penglihatan malaikat-malaikat yang berkata bahwa Ia hidup –Lukas 24:22-23. Tak ada yang suka ketinggalan. Bahkan, psikologi telah menemukan gangguan baru—FOMO (fear of missing out, takut ketinggalan). Kabar yang dibawa para perempuan itu adalah kabar baik dan perubahan peristiwa yang menakjubkan, namun itu tidak membawa sukacita kepada yang lain karena itu tidak terjadi pada mereka. Kabar baik jarang menembus orang yang tenggelam dalam rasa kasihan terhadap diri sendiri dan Elia adalah salah satunya. Malam gelapnya datang berurutan setelah kemenangan menakjubkan di Gunung Karmel melawan nabi-nabi Baal. Tetapi dalam kegelapan perasaannya sendiri …ia meminta kepada Allah supaya nyawanya diambil; katanya: "Cukuplah sekarang, ya TUHAN, ambillah nyawaku, sebab aku bukan lebih baik daripada nenek moyangku –1 Raja-raja 19:4.

…Perasaan Gagal

Dan beberapa orang yang bersama-sama dengan kami pergi ke kubur itu, lalu melihat yang demikian seperti yang telah dikatakan perempuan-perempuan itu; tetapi Ia tidak mereka lihat –Lukas 24:24. Mudah untuk berpikir, "Itu berhasil bagi mereka tetapi tidak untukku." Walaupun usaha yang tidak berhasil dapat mengecilkan hati kita, bukan berarti itu kegagalan di pihak kita. Yohanes Pembaptis dengan setia menyerukan pertobatan kepada orang-orang, membaptis Kristus, dan menyaksikan suara yang mengguruh dari surga. Ia dengan tepat mengumumkan Mesias yang akan datang dan menunjuk murid-muridnya kepada …Anak domba Allah yang menghapus dosa dunia –Yohanes 1:29. Pelayanan ini membawanya ke tempat yang aman di sel penjara yang gelap. Ia sudah terbiasa dengan minimnya penghiburan dan makanan yang sedikit, tetapi yang membawa dia kepada keraguan gelap adalah perasaan ditinggalkan sepenuhnya oleh Allah. Dan Yohanes memanggil dua orang muridnya, lalu mengutus mereka kepada Yesus, berkata: "Engkah Dia yang harus datang, atau patutkah kami menantikan seorang lain?" –Lukas 7:19.

"Apakah aku salah?" Dalam kegelapan ia mulai mengalami hidup di punggung tanda tanya yang miring. John Bunyan menggambarkannya sebagai lumpur keputusasaan. Ini mungkin tampak seperti D-Day bagi orang Kristen, tetapi penekanan yang berlebihan pada upaya kita yang gagal tidak menghasilkan kebangkitan.

Kesimpulan

Tidak semua kegelapan rohani sepenuhnya dapat dihindari. Tidak setiap pengalaman rohani adalah saat berkat yang menghangatkan hati, demikian pula tidak setiap tempat. Ada masa-masa penganiayaan dan pencobaan yang dirancang untuk membawa orang-orang kudus kepada perhitungan jiwa yang hanya malam-malam gelap dapat melayaninya. Yesus sendiri dicobai dengan cara yang serupa dengan kita, ketika dalam kegelapan yang melingkupi pada jam kesembilan di kayu salib, suara-Nya bergema …dengan suara nyaring berkata: "Eli, Eli, lama sabaktani? yang berarti: Allah-Ku, Allah-Ku, mengapa Engkau meninggalkan Aku?" –Matius 27:46.

Jalan ke Emmaus menjadi saksi bahwa keberadaan iman yang hidup sama sekali tidak menjamin ketiadaan depresi rohani. Itu adalah kisah tentang orang-orang nyata dengan iman nyata yang mengalami pencobaan nyata. Ini membantu kita belajar bahwa bahkan kesenangan rohani tidak seharusnya dipegang terlalu erat. Penglihatan kita yang penuh keyakinan untuk masa depan, baik yang langsung maupun jangka panjang, harus dicelupkan dalam api kerendahan hati. Malam gelap adalah tempat di mana penipuan diri semacam itu mati, dan pengetahuan intim tentang Allah dilahirkan. Ia memindahkan kita dari mengasihi Allah karena berkat yang Ia berikan kepada mengasihi Allah karena hubungan kita dengan-Nya dan persekutuan yang menyertainya.

Sahabat perjalanan Kleopas tidak pernah disebutkan namanya. Ada yang berpendapat itu istrinya. Ada yang mengklaim itu Lukas. Tetapi identitas mereka dihilangkan, mungkin supaya kita lebih cenderung mengisi kekosongan itu dengan nama kita sendiri. Tujuh mil dari Yerusalem kita tersandung pada kenyataan pahit tentang siapa Juruselamat sesungguhnya dan bahwa keselamatan lebih dari sekadar cap karet yang menandai kepemilikan-Nya. Timbangan itu jatuh dari mata kita dan malam gelap jiwa memberi jalan kepada terangnya cahaya tengah hari kehadiran Allah. Saat itulah kita membuat lari gembira kembali ke kota damai hanya untuk sekali lagi disalahpahami. Dan mereka pergi dan memberitahukan itu kepada yang lain: tetapi mereka tidak percaya kepada mereka –Markus 16:13.

Dan demikianlah, aku heran pula pada manfaat menuliskan pikiran-pikiran semacam ini. Ini bukan perjumpaan yang dapat direkayasa dan dipahami secara intelektual. Ini adalah pertemuan yang sangat pribadi dengan Allah dan dibuat khusus untuk tiap individu. Tetapi mungkin kita, dalam generasi yang dangkal ini, dapat didorong untuk meraih dan merangkul kegelapan daripada menemuinya dengan penolakan yang penuh kebencian. Dan di sana, dalam kegelapan malam yang mengancam, belajar merangkul Juruselamat terang.

Lamanya jiwaku terkurung,
Terikat rapat dalam dosa dan malam kodrat.
Matamu memancarkan sinar yang menghidupkan,
Aku terjaga; penjara menyala dalam terang.
Rantainya jatuh. Hatiku bebas.
Aku bangkit, keluar, dan mengikut Engkau.

- Charles Wesley

I stepped quietly down the stairs, my eyes groggy. It was midnight and a soft light glowed from my parents’ room. My new baby brother was crying, probably what had woken me up at this hour, and I decided to check up on Mom and wee baby.

My mother was picking him up, crooning softly. I expected her to look weary. Instead, her eyes were sparkling with delight as she exclaimed, “Oh, he’s just hungry!” She settled into the rocking chair and soon the house was restored to its midnight quiet.

Her joy at getting up in the middle of the night to feed her baby made a deep impression on my 18-year-old mind. She gave me the unspoken message that this baby was wanted and loved, and she found deep delight in caring for him. This was her ninth baby and I had often seen this in my mother, but this time it felt extra special.

Was my mother deprived of a fulfilling life?

Throughout history the role of a woman and motherhood has been evaluated and reevaluated; respected and demonized by turn. In the early 1900s, girls dreamed of becoming a mother just as their mothers and grandmothers before them. By the 1970s, the centuries’-old classic role of women was under attack. As one woman wrote, “I was busy raising my four children. These were the happiest years of my life, and we were shocked to suddenly hear that mothering only takes a third-grade education and a fulltime mother is unnecessary. Mothers who were applauded by society were suddenly bombarded with a new buzzword—fullfillment.”1

Today, according to some online reports, roughly 27% of infants and toddlers in America are placed in some form of paid childcare arrangement. Many of these mothers say they are happier and healthier on the job than they are at home with their children. Perhaps they are happier because taking on a challenge provides a sense of well-being, rather than living “discontentedly” at home. God’s will is that women of God would find their deepest joy and fulfillment in their home and with their children.

The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things; That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed –Titus 2:3-5.

In the past, the term “a keeper at home” had a more clearly understood and defined definition. Today we can stay at home and yet still be consumed with …wandering about from house to house… –1 Timothy 5:13, on our phones. In 2 Timothy, Paul continues … This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves… –2 Timothy 3:1-2. How much of my messaging and communication is consumed with loving myself? Technology can be a useful tool, but it can also become a distracting vice and addiction. It can also be a source of depression and discouragement if my house, décor, birthday cakes, or holidays are compared with all the perfect accomplishments of others. Choosing to stay at home in your focuses and thoughts produces peace and contentment.

God says, Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward –Psalm 127:3. Our children are His heritage and His reward! In a noisy world, full of other distractions, let’s not lose sight of this.

We want to keep a mother’s role respected and well-defined. But even in the church, time and technology are changing things and a subtle influence has crept in. Lucrative online businesses grab our attention, breeding a subtle discontent. “Me time” and “self-care” have become buzzwords and we are fascinated with new culture fads like coffee shops and shopping malls, each of which can take focus and energy away from our children. For some, it is easier to focus on the newest décor or an affluent lifestyle rather than a large family.

While some may question or wish to debate how many children are too many, or too little, let’s remember that God has given us some clear principles on this issue. Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward. As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth. Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate –Psalm 127:3-5. The Scripture passages that speak about children show us that God’s view regarding children is quite different from the prevailing view that many have in our world today.

An even more subtle question that I see young women wrestling with is this: “Is it more spiritual to be involved in ministry rather than to bring more children into the world?” I wrestled through this question as a young mother. All my work in the house was done with a subconscious “I’ll get this done quickly and then I’ll have time for more important things.” But when I look at the example of older, godly mothers, I see that their home and children were their important work—their focus.

My calling as a mother is not an inferior calling. A peaceful home is an oasis for hurting people and few things are as refreshing and beautiful as children who are loved and “trained up” in the ways of God. An orderly happy family is a powerful witness to our communities, and it is one way truth is propagated. It is not a choice between family or ministry, but rather family is ministry and together we can minister to others. No, it is not a ministry that all are called to; some are called to singleness, while others go through the difficulty of infertility. In each of these we are called to a selfless life of service to God and others.

Elisabeth Elliot said, “The process of shaping the child, shapes also the mother herself. Reverence for her sacred burden calls her to all that is pure and good, that she may teach primarily by her own humble, daily example.”2 Reverence—first to God and then to our sacred calling—allows our own souls to be purified as we live in obedience to this calling.

In these busy years, it is easy to feel overwhelmed and discouraged with the daily responsibilities, but God sees the big picture of what is being accomplished. It is infinitely more glorious than the messy floors and hungry tummies that I see. He sees the souls being birthed and raised, each one as a potential soldier in His kingdom. He sees what He is doing in our hearts as we learn to unselfishly give to our families. He is actively involved, even when all I can see is the challenge of today.

Eventually, the child-bearing and child-raising years are over. Children grow up and leave home. Then what? In Titus 2, godly older women are described as …teachers of good things –Titus 2:3. They are given the directive: That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed –Titus 2:4-5.

Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence. For Adam was first formed, then Eve –1 Timothy 2:11-13. Just as Paul instructs us, we believe in women being silent in the church, but this doesn’t mean that women are to be silent in all situations, places, and relationships. God has an important ministry for older women who have learned valuable life lessons and have the ability to encourage and disciple the younger generation. The younger women also have an important ministry …to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed –Titus 2:4-5.

God doesn’t need perfect women to teach the younger, rather He wants those who are honest, humble, and willing. Often the best advice is born out of experience. If you have made mistakes in your marriage, if you have gone through infertility or grief and have come out as a better person, you are all the more qualified to disciple a younger woman. Experience brings compassion for another’s pain and equips you to understand and articulate the path forward for a struggling younger woman.

I hear the cry of younger women desiring to have an older sister walk beside them, but I also see older women shrinking from the task. Can we change this? Perhaps it has never been your habit to engage in heart sharing. Perhaps you struggle with fear as you think of being vulnerable. Perhaps you feel like you don’t have the time it takes to include others in your life. These hindrances are common to us all, but we can, by the grace of God, push past these fears and fulfill God’s will for us as women.

  • Reach out and ask. Don’t always wait until someone pursues you. Choose one younger woman to befriend and learn the inner thoughts and questions of her heart. If you have never learned how to be vulnerable in your relationships, ask God to teach you. And He will.
  • Start with small gestures of encouragement and love. These will grow into relationships, and opportunities to influence.
  • Be willing to sacrifice your time. Ministry is a lifestyle of caring more about others than ourselves. God needs us to be willing to use our voice. It is His way for us to reproduce our spiritual values and bless the next generation.

Teaching others about the things of God strengthens everyone involved—the teacher and the disciple. Truth, dissected and taught, settles into the heart. Don’t believe the lie that we don't need spiritual vulnerability with each other. We do need it since it is vital for our on-going growth and maturity. It is also vital for the health of the church and for the next generation.

Busy young mother or older woman, whatever stage of life you’re in, God has given you the tools through His spirit to be an influence for good in the lives of those around you.

And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not –Galatians 6:9.

Nilipanda ngazi kwa upole, macho yangu yalikuwa yamechoka. Ilikuwa saa sita usiku na mwanga laini ulikuwa ukimutiririka kutoka katika chumba cha wazazi wangu. Kaka yangu mchanga alikuwa akilia, labda ndiyo aliyenifanya nimeamka saa hii, hivyo nikamua kuangalia Mama na mtoto mdogo.

Mama alikuwa akimmwinua, akimwimbia kwa sauti laini. Nilitarajia aanze kuonekana mchovu. Badala yake, macho yake yalikuwa yakileng'aa kwa furaha aliposema, “Ah, yupo tu na njaa!” Alikaa kwenye kiti cha kupiga mswaki na hivi karibuni nyumba ikarudishwa katika utulivu wa usiku.

Furaha yake ya kuinuka katikati ya usiku kumlisha mtoto ilinishika kwa nguvu akilini mwangu wa miaka 18. Alinipa ujumbe usiokuwa wa maneno kwamba mtoto huyu alihitajika na kupendwa, na alipata furaha kubwa katika kumtunza. Huyu alikuwa mtoto wake wa tisa na mara nyingi nilimuona mama akifanya hivi, lakini wakati huu ilihisi maalum zaidi.

Je, mama yangu alikosa maisha yenye kufaa?

Kupitia historia, nafasi ya mwanamke na uunguzi wa uzazi vimekuwa vikitathminiwa na kutathminiwa tena; kupewa heshima na kuhukumiwa kwa mabadiliko. Mwanzoni mwa karne ya 1900, wasichana waliota kuwa mama kama ilivyokuwa kwa mama zao na bibi zao kabla yao. Kufikia miaka ya 1970, nafasi ya jadi ya wanawake iliyoendelea kwa karne nyingi ilikuwa ikiangaziwa. Kama mwanamke mmoja alivyoandika, “Nilikuwa nikijishughulisha na kulea watoto wangu wanne. Haya yalikuwa miaka ya furaha zaidi maishani mwangu, na tulikanushwa kushtuka kusikia ghafla kwamba kulea watoto kunahitaji tu elimu ya daraja la tatu na mama wa wakati wote haitegemeiwi. Mama waliokuwa wakisifiwa na jamii ghafla walipigwa na neno jipya—utekelezaji.”1

Leo, kulingana na ripoti fulani mtandaoni, takriban 27% ya watoto wachanga na watoto wadogo nchini Amerika wanawekwa katika aina fulani ya malezi ya kulipwa. Mama wengi wa aina hii wanasema wanahisi furaha zaidi na afya bora kazini kuliko walivyo nyumbani na watoto wao. Labda wanafurahia kwa sababu kukumbatia changamoto kunaleta hisia ya ustawi, badala ya kuishi “wakikaidi” nyumbani. Mapenzi ya Mungu ni kwamba wanawake wa Mungu wapate furaha zao za ndani na utimilifu wa maisha yao nyumbani na pamoja na watoto wao.

Wanawake waliozeeka nao hao wawe katika mwenendo unaofaa utakatifu, si wa kupoteza sifa, wasio wanywaji wa pombe mwingi, walifundisha mambo mema; ili waweke wanawake wajana kuwa warudifu, wapendao wake, wapendao watoto wao, wawe wa busara, wakiwa wasafi, walinzi wa nyumbani, wema, wakiwa watiifu kwa wake zao wenyewe, ili neno la Mungu lisizwemezee –Tito 2:3-5.

Kwakati uliopita, neno “mlezi wa nyumbani” lilikuwa na ufafanuzi ulioeleweka zaidi na uliodhanishwa. Leo tunaweza kukaa nyumbani na bado tukawa tumekazwa na …kutembea kutoka nyumba hadi nyumba… –1 Timotheo 5:13, kwa simu zetu. Katika 2 Timotheo, Paulo anaendelea … Jua hili pia, kwamba nyakati za hatari zitatokea wakati wa mwisho. Kwa kuwa watu watakuwa wanawapenda wao wenyewe… –2 Timotheo 3:1-2. Ni kiasi gani ya ujumbe wangu na mawasiliano yangu yanajazwa na kujipenda? Teknolojia inaweza kuwa chombo cha manufaa, lakini pia inaweza kuwa adhabu ya kukuvutia na uraibu. Pia inaweza kuwa chanzo cha msongo wa mawazo na kukata tamaa ikiwa nyumbani kwangu, mapambo, bakesi za siku za kuzaliwa, au sikukuu zitatolinganishwa na mafanikio kamili ya wengine. Kuchagua kukaa nyumbani kwa mawazo na fikra zako huleta amani na kuridhika.

Mungu anasema, Tazama, watoto ni urithi wa BWANA: na tunda la tumbo ni zawadi yake –Zaburi 127:3. Watoto wetu ni urithi wake na zawadi yake! Katika ulimwengu wenye kelele, uliojaa vishawishi vingine, tusipoteze hili machoni.

Tunataka nafasi ya mama iheshimiwa na iainishwe vyema. Lakini hata kanisani, wakati na teknolojia yanabadilisha mambo na ushawishi mwororo umeingia polepole. Biashara za mtandaoni zenye faida zinavutia hisia zetu, zikileta kukosa kuridhika kidogo. “Wakati wangu” na “kujijali” vimekuwa maneno ya mtindo na tunashawishika na mitindo mipya ya utamaduni kama maduka ya kahawa na maduka makubwa, ambayo kila moja inaweza kuondoa umakini na nguvu kutoka kwa watoto wetu. Kwa wengine, ni rahisi zaidi kuangazia mapambo mapya au mtindo wa maisha wa kifahari badala ya familia kubwa.

Wakati wengine wanaweza kuuliza au kutaka kujadili ni watoto wangapi ni wengi kupita kiasi, au ni wangapi ni wachache, tukumbuke kwamba Mungu ametupa kanuni wazi juu ya suala hili. Tazama, watoto ni urithi wa BWANA: na tunda la tumbo ni zawadi yake. Kama mishale iko mkononi mwa mtu mwenye nguvu; ndivyo watoto wa ujana. Heri ya mtu aliye na bofia yake imejaa: hawatajisikia aibu, bali watazungumza na maadui mlangoni –Zaburi 127:3-5. Mistari ya Maandiko yanayozungumzia watoto yanaonyesha kwetu kwamba mtazamo wa Mungu kuhusu watoto ni tofauti sana na mtazamo wa wengi katika dunia yetu ya leo.

Swali moja hata nyeti zaidi ambalo ninaona wanawake vijana wakilitafuta ni hili: “Je, ni kiroho zaidi kushiriki huduma kuliko kuleta watoto zaidi duniani?” Nilijaribu kupitia swali hili kama mama mchanga. Kazi zangu zote za nyumbani zilifanywa kwa mawazo yasiyo wazi “Nitafanya hivi haraka kisha nitakuwa na muda wa mambo muhimu zaidi.” Lakini ninapotazama mfano wa mama wazee wa Mungu, naona nyumba yao na watoto wao walikuwa kazi yao muhimu—umakini wao.

Wito wangu kama mama si wito wa chini. Nyumba yenye amani ni oasia kwa watu waliodhulumiwa na vitu vyengine ni vichache vinavyofanya kupendeza na uzuri kama watoto waliopendwa na “kuwekwa katika njia” za Mungu. Familia iliyo na mpangilio na yenye furaha ni ushuhuda wenye nguvu kwa jumuiya zetu, na ni njia moja ukweli unavyosambazwa. Si uamuzi kati ya familia au huduma, bali familia ni huduma na pamoja tunaweza kuhudumia wengine. Hapana, si huduma ambayo wote wameitwa kufanya; baadhi wameitwa kutobalehe kwa ndoa, wakati wengine hupitia ugumu wa kutokuweza kuwa na watoto. Katika hizi zote tumeitwa kuishi maisha yasiyo ya ubinafsi ya kumtumikia Mungu na wengine.

Elisabeth Elliot alisema, “Mchakato wa kumfanya mtoto, huwafanya pia mama mwenyewe. Kuogopa mzigo wake mtakatifu humwita kufanya yote yaliyo takatifu na mema, ili afundishe hasa kwa mfano wake mdogo, wa kila siku.”2 Heshima—kwanza kwa Mungu na kisha kwa wito wetu mtakatifu—huwezesha nafsi zetu kujisafisha tunapoishi kwa utii wa wito huu.

Katikati ya miaka hii yenye shughuli nyingi, ni rahisi kuhisi kuzidiwa na kukatishwa tamaa kutokana na majukumu ya kila siku, lakini Mungu anaona picha kubwa ya kile kinachofanywa. Ni zaidi ya utukufu kuliko sakafu zilizochanganyikana na tumbo za njaa ninazoona. Anaona roho zinazozaa na kulelewa, kila moja kama askari anayewezekana katika ufalme Wake. Anaona kile anachofanya mioyoni mwetu tunapojifunza kutoa bila kujichukulia wenyewe. Yuko mhenjani hata wakati ninachoweza kuona ni changamoto ya leo tu.

Mwishowe, miaka ya kuzaa na kulea yatakapokamilika. Watoto hukua na kuondoka nyumbani. Basi je, kisha? Katika Tito 2, wanawake waliozeeka wa Mungu wanaelezewa kama …walifundisha mambo mema –Tito 2:3. Wanapewa maagizo: Ili wawe wa kufundisha wanawake wajana kuwa warudifu, wapendao wake, wapendao watoto wao, wawe wa busara, wakiwa wasafi, walinzi wa nyumbani, wema, wakiwa watiifu kwa wake zao wenyewe, ili neno la Mungu lisizwemezee –Tito 2:4-5.

Mwanamke ajifunze kimya kwa uzito wote. Lakini siwachukui wanawake kufundisha, wala kuchukua mamlaka juu ya mwanaume, bali wawe kimya. Kwa kuwa Adamu aliumbwa kwanza, kisha Eva –1 Timotheo 2:11-13. Kama Paulo anatuagiza, tunaamini wanawake wawe kimya kanisani, lakini hii haimaanishi wanawake watulie kimya katika kila hali, mahali na uhusiano wote. Mungu ana huduma muhimu kwa wanawake waliozeeka ambao wamejifunza masomo ya maisha na wana uwezo wa kuhimiza na kumkufuza kizazi kipya. Wanawake vijana pia wana huduma muhimu …kuwa warudifu, wapendao wake, wapendao watoto wao, wawe wa busara, wakiwa wasafi, walinzi wa nyumbani, wema, wakiwa watiifu kwa wake zao wenyewe, ili neno la Mungu lisizwemezee –Tito 2:4-5.

Mungu hahitaji wanawake kamili kufundisha wajana, badala yake anataka wale wenye uaminifu, unyenyekevu, na utayari. Mara nyingi ushauri bora unatokana na uzoefu. Ikiwa umefanya makosa katika ndoa yako, ikiwa umepitia kutoweza kuzaa au majonzi na umejitokeza kuwa mtu bora, basi wewe umehitimu zaidi kuwafundisha wanawake wachanga. Uzoefu huleta huruma kwa maumivu ya mwingine na kukuwezesha kuelewa na kuzungumza njia ya mbele kwa mwanamke mchanga anayejaribu.

Nasikia kilio cha wanawake vijana wakitamani kupewa dada mzee aliyesimama nao, lakini pia naona wanawake wazee wakinzwa na kazi hiyo. Je, tunaweza kubadilisha hili? Labda haijawahi kuwa tabia yako kushiriki kwa moyo. Labda unakumbana na hofu unapofikiria kuwa wazi. Labda unahisi huna muda wa kumjumuisha mwingine katika maisha yako. Vizuizi hivi ni kawaida kwa sisi sote, lakini kwa neema ya Mungu tunaweza kupitiliza hofu hizi na kutimiza mapenzi ya Mungu kwetu kama wanawake.

  • Fikia na ulaze ombi. Usisubiri kila mara mpaka mtu akutafute. Chagua mwanamke mdogo mmoja kuwa rafiki na ujifunze mawazo ya ndani na maswali ya moyo wake. Ikiwa hujawahi kujifunza jinsi ya kuwa dhaifu katika mahusiano yako, muombe Mungu akuonyeshe. Na Atakufundisha.
  • Anza kwa vitendo vidogo vya himizo na upendo. Haya yatajengwa kuwa uhusiano, na fursa za kuathiri.
  • Kubali ku sacrifica muda wako. Huduma ni mtindo wa maisha wa kumjali wengine zaidi kuliko sisi wenyewe. Mungu anahitaji tuwe tayari kutumia sauti yetu. Hii ni njia yake ya kutuzalisha thamani zetu za kiroho na kubariki kizazi kijacho.

Kumfundisha mwingine kuhusu mambo ya Mungu kunaimarisha wote waliotoa—mwalimu na mwanafunzi. Ukweli, ukichambuliwa na kufundishwa, unakaa moyoni. Usiamini uwongo kwamba hatuhitaji uzito wa kiroho kati yetu. Tunauhitaji kwa kuwa ni muhimu kwa ukuaji wetu unaoendelea na kukomaa. Pia ni muhimu kwa afya ya kanisa na kwa kizazi kijacho.

Mama mchanga mwenye shughuli nyingi au mwanamke mzee, hatua yoyote ya maisha uliyomo, Mungu amekupa zana kupitia Roho Yake kuwa ushawishi mwema katika maisha ya wale walikuzunguka.

Na tusichoke kufanya mema: kwa kuwa kwa wakati wake tutavuna, tusiomezwa moyo –Wagalatia 6:9.

And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these
that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? –Luke 24:17.

On June 6, 1944, 156,000 American, British, and Canadian troops landed on a 50-mile stretch of beach in Normandy, France. After several months of intense fighting, they overcame the initial defenses and swarmed into the German-held territory. The surprise attack, known as D-Day, caught the Germans off guard. However, it wasn’t until March of the next year that France was finally liberated from German forces. D-day was the beginning of the end of World War II on the western front and it was the event that seemed to sap the life from the notorious German army, from which they never recovered. It appears rather coincidental that so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.

I can imagine that these two believers, plodding upon the road to Emmaus that dim and dismal evening, were feeling a little the same way. Their D-Day had arrived totally unexpected. I would suspect that every living person has at one time or another experienced moments of intense sadness—their own D-day, so-to-speak. Even some animals have been known to express a melancholy mood at the death of their master or mate. But these two disciples seemed to be experiencing a pain far beyond the normal loss of a friend. They were staring into the face of the grim reality that all their bright hopes of a shining tomorrow were hopelessly shattered in a ruinous heap at the foot of the cross.

This agony was no ordinary fit of depression but rather it was a depression linked to a crisis of faith. This type of discouragement is a state of intense spiritual anguish in which the struggling, despairing believer feels he is abandoned by God. It is a hopeless feeling that the sun of God's blessedness has been eclipsed and the dark night of the soul has become a permanent resident within.

While all of us seek to valiantly resist such dark temptations, a brief search into the lives of many godly men will reveal that these temptations are very real and are quite common to man. In such a condition, life seems impossible and the impending gloom that has settled upon the heart sees no light at the end of the tunnel. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed? wilt thou be altogether unto me as a liar, and as waters that fail? –Jeremiah 15:18. This is obviously an overstated exaggeration that escaped the lips of the weeping prophet, but it gives us a direct snapshot into the dreaded pain in the depths of his soul.

For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:8-9. This dark night of the soul shows no respect to persons. It invades the lives of princes and paupers, preachers and penitents, public and private people, pulpits and pews. These two disciples had verbally revisited every possible scenario in their journey along the Emmaus Road. They had no doubt found plenty of fault in others as well as personal regret. The “what ifs” and “if onlys” had thoroughly been discussed, but nothing could reverse the outcome and their restless anxiety lingered still.

The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs or approximately seven miles. And along this doleful journey a Stranger joined ranks with the distraught duo in their D-Day and asked them for an account of their sadness. But he is no curious onlooker. He is the risen Lord who has come to cast His heavenly light upon our darkened pathway. Rather than revealing Himself abruptly, and perhaps for our benefit, he patiently allows them to expose the depleted spiritual road that they were treading upon.

Thus, the conversation unfolds as the mile markers pass, each revealing our sincere erroneous efforts that lead us further from the city of peace and into the dark night of the soul…

…The Ignorance of Others

And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? –Luke 24:18. Ask any stranger on the streets of New York City why the flags were flying at half-mast three days after the towers fell on September 11, and you would receive the same incredulous answer ascribed to these two. “How can you be so ignorant?” We all tend to marvel at people who do not hold the same knowledge that we imagine ourselves to possess. The younger the man, the more answers that he believes the coffers of his understanding hold.

This is nothing new. Moses, as a young man, …supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not –Acts 7:25. While he firmly understood that he owned the plan of God, he was badly mistaken in the percentage that he possessed. If our recourse cannot rectify the given situation, our answers are not the real answer. The heartfelt disdain that naturally arises toward those who see it differently is the beginning marker that we are on the wrong path. Miles down the pathway of life, Moses began to feel the desperation of that pain and the darkness of the hour. I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me. And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness –Numbers 11:14-15. Why did Moses not see this earlier in life? For the same cause that these two fervent disciples’ …eyes were holden that they should not know him –Luke 24:16.

…Reason

And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people –Luke 24:19. They had their private perception of who the Christ was, but they were seeing …through a glass, darkly… –1 Corinthians 13:12. Their partial knowledge was leaning heavily on their own understanding and looking for the wrong kind of redemption. To them, their redeemer was (past tense) a prophet that no longer could do what they wanted him to do. We all want Jesus to solve our problems and make us feel better, but His purpose is to free us from our presumption and sin.

Jacob had every reason to believe that the birthright and blessing was to be his. At Bethel, God had promised to bless him. Jacob reckoned this to arrive in a material format. And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God –Genesis 28:20-21.

But the greatest blessing he ever received from God arrived to him on the wings of a deep dark night. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him. And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed –Genesis 32:24-28.

Jacob had already accumulated an abundance of earthly possessions. What more could he want? It was a dark night for Jacob when he discovered that he’d spent his life pursuing possessions and resisting God. He now seeks godly character and spiritual affluence. His victory was through surrender, and he limped away as a cripple with a crown. The Lord cannot fully bless a man until He has first conquered his powers of reason.

…Ill Fate

And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him –Luke 24:20. God specializes in turning grave dilemmas into monumental victories. Still, man looks around him and curses the darkness about him. Though there may be a volley of good reciprocating them, …the morning is to them even as the shadow of death… –Job 24:17. To give undo emphasis upon the evil about us is to mock the divinity of God. While we all may regret at times things that we could have done or said differently, we must invariably leave the results in the hands of God. Job experienced as much ill fate as anybody. So much so that he opened …his mouth, and cursed his day. And Job spake, and said, Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived. Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it. Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. As for that night, let darkness seize upon it… –Job 3:1-6. But somewhere before the dark events were rectified and lifted, the light shined into his soul, and he laid his hand to his mouth and worshiped.

…Personal Agenda

But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel… –Luke 24:21. It is but natural to attempt to understand any given situation and these two had selected the correct equation. Their folly lay in the presumption of the means that Christ was to perform this and the type of redemption they were to receive. They were looking forward to the day when their nation would be exalted over the Romans. When we unwittingly seek our own security, it is bound to lead to bitter disappointment. Naaman thought …He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper –2 Kings 5:11.

Abraham was promised the land of Canaan and he asked for a confirmation. He then prepared the covenant sacrifice prescribed by God, but the entire day passed, and God did nothing with them. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. –Genesis 15:12.

As Abraham waited on God to receive his offering, he continued to beat back the birds of prey. But as the day neared an end he began to feel abandoned by God and the dark night began to settle upon his soul. It takes a midnight experience for things to get dark enough for us to see the stars and quiet enough to hear His voice. But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:9.

…Impatience

…And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done –Luke 24:21. Many of us are disciplined enough to hold out for a season. It is when our hope is deferred (see Proverbs 13:12) that our hearts grow sick and faint. Three days seemed like a long time to these two. But three days, weeks, months, years, or even decades are all within the disposal of God’s clock. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? –Psalm 13:1.

Joseph patiently endured the ill treatment of his brothers and Potiphar, but the dungeon got long, and he entreated the butler to send for him when he was restored his position. But it was two full years (Genesis 41:1) until Pharoah dreamed and Joseph was finally hailed forth. But it was not so much the fault of the butler as it was the will of God who had called Joseph to be …laid in iron: Until the time that his word came: the word of the LORD tried him –Psalm 105:18-19. There is no more effective avenue to teach us patience than the discipline of darkness, from which few saints are exempt.

…Self-Pity

Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre; And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive –Luke 24:22-23. No one enjoys missing out. In fact, psychology has uncovered a new disorder –FOMO (fear of missing out). The tidings brought by the women was good news and an amazing turn of events, yet it brought the others no joy for it did not happen to them. Good news can rarely penetrate a person immersed in self-pity and Elijah was one such. His dark night arrived on the heels of a breathtaking triumph on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal. But in the blackness of his own inner feelings …he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers –1 Kings 19:4.

…Feelings of Failure

And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not –Luke 24:24. It is easy to think, “It worked for them but it’s not working for me.” While unsuccessful efforts may discourage us, it is not necessarily a failure on our part. John the Baptist had faithfully called the people to repentance, baptized Christ, and witnessed the thundering voice from heaven. He accurately announced the coming Messiah and pointed his disciples to …the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world –John 1:29. This ministry earned him a secure place in a dark prison cell. He had been well accustomed to the lack of comfort and a meager diet, but it was the feelings of utter abandonment by God that brought him unto dark doubts. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? –Luke 7:19.

“Was I wrong?” In the darkness he began to experience life on the sloping back of a question mark. John Bunyan describes it as the slough of despond. It may appear like D-Day for the Christian, but undue emphasis upon our unsuccessful efforts promotes no resurrection.

Conclusion

Not all spiritual darkness is completely avoidable. Not every spiritual experience is a time of heartfelt blessing, nor is every place. There are times of persecution and testing that are designed to bring saints unto the soul reckoning that only dark nights can minister unto. Jesus Himself was tempted in a similar manner to us, when in the pervading darkness of the ninth hour on the cross, His voice rang out …with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? –Matthew 27:46.

The road to Emmaus bears witness to the fact that a vibrant existence of faith gives no guarantee of the absence of spiritual depression. It is a story about real people with real faith experiencing real trials. It is helpful to teach us that even spiritual pleasures ought not to be held too tightly. Our confident visions for the future both immediate and long term must be immersed in the fires of humility. The dark night is the place where such self-deception dies, and an intimate knowledge of God is birthed. It transitions us from loving God for the blessings He gives us, to loving God for our relationship with Him and the communion that follows.

The traveling companion of Cleopas was never mentioned. Some think it was his wife. Some claim it was Luke. But their identity was omitted, perhaps so that we might be more apt to fill the vacancy with our own name. Seven miles from Jerusalem we stumble upon the stark reality of whom the Savior really is and that salvation is more than just a rubber stamp marking His possession. The scales fall from our eyes and the dark night of the soul gives way to the brightness of the noonday light of the presence of God. It is then that we make our joyous dash back to the city of peace only to be misunderstood again. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them –Mark 16:13.

And so, I wonder even at the profitability of writing down such thoughts. It is not an encounter that can be manufactured and intellectually understood. It is a highly personal convocation with God and tailored specifically to each individual. But perhaps we, in our shallow generation, can be encouraged to reach out and embrace the darkness instead of meeting it with a loathing resistance. And there in the menacing darkness of night, learn to embrace the Savior of light.

Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature's night.
Thine eye diffused a quickening ray,
I woke; the dungeon flamed with light.
My chains fell off. My heart was free.
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

- Charles Wesley
