And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these
that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? –Luke 24:17.

On June 6, 1944, 156,000 American, British, and Canadian troops landed on a 50-mile stretch of beach in Normandy, France. After several months of intense fighting, they overcame the initial defenses and swarmed into the German-held territory. The surprise attack, known as D-Day, caught the Germans off guard. However, it wasn’t until March of the next year that France was finally liberated from German forces. D-day was the beginning of the end of World War II on the western front and it was the event that seemed to sap the life from the notorious German army, from which they never recovered. It appears rather coincidental that so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.

I can imagine that these two believers, plodding upon the road to Emmaus that dim and dismal evening, were feeling a little the same way. Their D-Day had arrived totally unexpected. I would suspect that every living person has at one time or another experienced moments of intense sadness—their own D-day, so-to-speak. Even some animals have been known to express a melancholy mood at the death of their master or mate. But these two disciples seemed to be experiencing a pain far beyond the normal loss of a friend. They were staring into the face of the grim reality that all their bright hopes of a shining tomorrow were hopelessly shattered in a ruinous heap at the foot of the cross.

This agony was no ordinary fit of depression but rather it was a depression linked to a crisis of faith. This type of discouragement is a state of intense spiritual anguish in which the struggling, despairing believer feels he is abandoned by God. It is a hopeless feeling that the sun of God's blessedness has been eclipsed and the dark night of the soul has become a permanent resident within.

While all of us seek to valiantly resist such dark temptations, a brief search into the lives of many godly men will reveal that these temptations are very real and are quite common to man. In such a condition, life seems impossible and the impending gloom that has settled upon the heart sees no light at the end of the tunnel. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed? wilt thou be altogether unto me as a liar, and as waters that fail? –Jeremiah 15:18. This is obviously an overstated exaggeration that escaped the lips of the weeping prophet, but it gives us a direct snapshot into the dreaded pain in the depths of his soul.

For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:8-9. This dark night of the soul shows no respect to persons. It invades the lives of princes and paupers, preachers and penitents, public and private people, pulpits and pews. These two disciples had verbally revisited every possible scenario in their journey along the Emmaus Road. They had no doubt found plenty of fault in others as well as personal regret. The “what ifs” and “if onlys” had thoroughly been discussed, but nothing could reverse the outcome and their restless anxiety lingered still.

The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs or approximately seven miles. And along this doleful journey a Stranger joined ranks with the distraught duo in their D-Day and asked them for an account of their sadness. But he is no curious onlooker. He is the risen Lord who has come to cast His heavenly light upon our darkened pathway. Rather than revealing Himself abruptly, and perhaps for our benefit, he patiently allows them to expose the depleted spiritual road that they were treading upon.

Thus, the conversation unfolds as the mile markers pass, each revealing our sincere erroneous efforts that lead us further from the city of peace and into the dark night of the soul…

…The Ignorance of Others

And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? –Luke 24:18. Ask any stranger on the streets of New York City why the flags were flying at half-mast three days after the towers fell on September 11, and you would receive the same incredulous answer ascribed to these two. “How can you be so ignorant?” We all tend to marvel at people who do not hold the same knowledge that we imagine ourselves to possess. The younger the man, the more answers that he believes the coffers of his understanding hold.

This is nothing new. Moses, as a young man, …supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not –Acts 7:25. While he firmly understood that he owned the plan of God, he was badly mistaken in the percentage that he possessed. If our recourse cannot rectify the given situation, our answers are not the real answer. The heartfelt disdain that naturally arises toward those who see it differently is the beginning marker that we are on the wrong path. Miles down the pathway of life, Moses began to feel the desperation of that pain and the darkness of the hour. I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me. And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness –Numbers 11:14-15. Why did Moses not see this earlier in life? For the same cause that these two fervent disciples’ …eyes were holden that they should not know him –Luke 24:16.

…Reason

And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people –Luke 24:19. They had their private perception of who the Christ was, but they were seeing …through a glass, darkly… –1 Corinthians 13:12. Their partial knowledge was leaning heavily on their own understanding and looking for the wrong kind of redemption. To them, their redeemer was (past tense) a prophet that no longer could do what they wanted him to do. We all want Jesus to solve our problems and make us feel better, but His purpose is to free us from our presumption and sin.

Jacob had every reason to believe that the birthright and blessing was to be his. At Bethel, God had promised to bless him. Jacob reckoned this to arrive in a material format. And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God –Genesis 28:20-21.

But the greatest blessing he ever received from God arrived to him on the wings of a deep dark night. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him. And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed –Genesis 32:24-28.

Jacob had already accumulated an abundance of earthly possessions. What more could he want? It was a dark night for Jacob when he discovered that he’d spent his life pursuing possessions and resisting God. He now seeks godly character and spiritual affluence. His victory was through surrender, and he limped away as a cripple with a crown. The Lord cannot fully bless a man until He has first conquered his powers of reason.

…Ill Fate

And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him –Luke 24:20. God specializes in turning grave dilemmas into monumental victories. Still, man looks around him and curses the darkness about him. Though there may be a volley of good reciprocating them, …the morning is to them even as the shadow of death… –Job 24:17. To give undo emphasis upon the evil about us is to mock the divinity of God. While we all may regret at times things that we could have done or said differently, we must invariably leave the results in the hands of God. Job experienced as much ill fate as anybody. So much so that he opened …his mouth, and cursed his day. And Job spake, and said, Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived. Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it. Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. As for that night, let darkness seize upon it… –Job 3:1-6. But somewhere before the dark events were rectified and lifted, the light shined into his soul, and he laid his hand to his mouth and worshiped.

…Personal Agenda

But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel… –Luke 24:21. It is but natural to attempt to understand any given situation and these two had selected the correct equation. Their folly lay in the presumption of the means that Christ was to perform this and the type of redemption they were to receive. They were looking forward to the day when their nation would be exalted over the Romans. When we unwittingly seek our own security, it is bound to lead to bitter disappointment. Naaman thought …He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper –2 Kings 5:11.

Abraham was promised the land of Canaan and he asked for a confirmation. He then prepared the covenant sacrifice prescribed by God, but the entire day passed, and God did nothing with them. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. –Genesis 15:12.

As Abraham waited on God to receive his offering, he continued to beat back the birds of prey. But as the day neared an end he began to feel abandoned by God and the dark night began to settle upon his soul. It takes a midnight experience for things to get dark enough for us to see the stars and quiet enough to hear His voice. But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:9.

…Impatience

…And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done –Luke 24:21. Many of us are disciplined enough to hold out for a season. It is when our hope is deferred (see Proverbs 13:12) that our hearts grow sick and faint. Three days seemed like a long time to these two. But three days, weeks, months, years, or even decades are all within the disposal of God’s clock. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? –Psalm 13:1.

Joseph patiently endured the ill treatment of his brothers and Potiphar, but the dungeon got long, and he entreated the butler to send for him when he was restored his position. But it was two full years (Genesis 41:1) until Pharoah dreamed and Joseph was finally hailed forth. But it was not so much the fault of the butler as it was the will of God who had called Joseph to be …laid in iron: Until the time that his word came: the word of the LORD tried him –Psalm 105:18-19. There is no more effective avenue to teach us patience than the discipline of darkness, from which few saints are exempt.

…Self-Pity

Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre; And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive –Luke 24:22-23. No one enjoys missing out. In fact, psychology has uncovered a new disorder –FOMO (fear of missing out). The tidings brought by the women was good news and an amazing turn of events, yet it brought the others no joy for it did not happen to them. Good news can rarely penetrate a person immersed in self-pity and Elijah was one such. His dark night arrived on the heels of a breathtaking triumph on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal. But in the blackness of his own inner feelings …he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers –1 Kings 19:4.

…Feelings of Failure

And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not –Luke 24:24. It is easy to think, “It worked for them but it’s not working for me.” While unsuccessful efforts may discourage us, it is not necessarily a failure on our part. John the Baptist had faithfully called the people to repentance, baptized Christ, and witnessed the thundering voice from heaven. He accurately announced the coming Messiah and pointed his disciples to …the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world –John 1:29. This ministry earned him a secure place in a dark prison cell. He had been well accustomed to the lack of comfort and a meager diet, but it was the feelings of utter abandonment by God that brought him unto dark doubts. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? –Luke 7:19.

“Was I wrong?” In the darkness he began to experience life on the sloping back of a question mark. John Bunyan describes it as the slough of despond. It may appear like D-Day for the Christian, but undue emphasis upon our unsuccessful efforts promotes no resurrection.

Conclusion

Not all spiritual darkness is completely avoidable. Not every spiritual experience is a time of heartfelt blessing, nor is every place. There are times of persecution and testing that are designed to bring saints unto the soul reckoning that only dark nights can minister unto. Jesus Himself was tempted in a similar manner to us, when in the pervading darkness of the ninth hour on the cross, His voice rang out …with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? –Matthew 27:46.

The road to Emmaus bears witness to the fact that a vibrant existence of faith gives no guarantee of the absence of spiritual depression. It is a story about real people with real faith experiencing real trials. It is helpful to teach us that even spiritual pleasures ought not to be held too tightly. Our confident visions for the future both immediate and long term must be immersed in the fires of humility. The dark night is the place where such self-deception dies, and an intimate knowledge of God is birthed. It transitions us from loving God for the blessings He gives us, to loving God for our relationship with Him and the communion that follows.

The traveling companion of Cleopas was never mentioned. Some think it was his wife. Some claim it was Luke. But their identity was omitted, perhaps so that we might be more apt to fill the vacancy with our own name. Seven miles from Jerusalem we stumble upon the stark reality of whom the Savior really is and that salvation is more than just a rubber stamp marking His possession. The scales fall from our eyes and the dark night of the soul gives way to the brightness of the noonday light of the presence of God. It is then that we make our joyous dash back to the city of peace only to be misunderstood again. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them –Mark 16:13.

And so, I wonder even at the profitability of writing down such thoughts. It is not an encounter that can be manufactured and intellectually understood. It is a highly personal convocation with God and tailored specifically to each individual. But perhaps we, in our shallow generation, can be encouraged to reach out and embrace the darkness instead of meeting it with a loathing resistance. And there in the menacing darkness of night, learn to embrace the Savior of light.

Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature's night.
Thine eye diffused a quickening ray,
I woke; the dungeon flamed with light.
My chains fell off. My heart was free.
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

- Charles Wesley

और उसने उनसे कहा, यह किस प्रकार की बातें हैं जो तुम एक दूसरे से करते हो
चलते-चलते और दुखी होते हुए? —लूका 24:17।

6 जून, 1944 को, 156,000 अमेरिकी, ब्रिटिश और कनाडाई सैनिकों ने नॉरमैंडी, फ्रांस के एक 50-मील तटरेखा पर कदम रखा। तीव्र लड़ाई के कई महीनों के बाद, उन्होंने प्रारंभिक रक्षा को पार किया और जर्मनी के कब्जे वाले इलाके में बह निकले। इस आश्चर्यजनक हमला, जिसे D-Day के नाम से जाना जाता है, ने जर्मनों को चौंका दिया। हालांकि, अगले वर्ष मार्च तक ही फ्रांस आखिरकार जर्मन सेनाओं से मुक्त हुआ। D-Day पश्चिमी मोर्चे पर द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध की समाप्ति की शुरुआत थी और यह वह घटना थी जिसने कुख्यात जर्मन सेना की शक्ति को कम कर दिया, जिससे वे कभी पूरी तरह पनपे नहीं। यह संयोग ही प्रतीत होता है कि इतने सारे नकारात्मक अर्थ वाले शब्द D अक्षर से शुरु होते हैं: निराशा, सन्देह, उदासी, विनाश, मोहभंग, हतोत्साह, उबासी, पराजय, अवसाद, निराशा, तबाही, छल, और मृत्यु।

मैं कल्पना कर सकता हूँ कि वे दो विश्वासी, उस उदास शाम को एम्माुस की राह पर चलते हुए, कुछ इसी तरह महसूस कर रहे थे। उनका D-Day बिल्कुल अप्रत्याशित रूप से आ गया था। मुझे संदेह है कि हर जीवित व्यक्ति ने कभी न कभी गहरी उदासी के क्षण अनुभव किए हैं—उनका अपना D-Day, एक प्रकार से। कुछ जानवरों को भी अपने स्वामी या साथी की मृत्‍यु पर शोक व्यक्त करते देखा गया है। परंतु ये दो चेलों को ऐसा दर्द किसी साधारण मित्र के खोने से कहीं अधिक गहरा प्रतीत हुआ। वे इस कठोर वास्तविकता का सामना कर रहे थे कि उनके सभी उज्जवल आशाएँ एक सुनहरी कल की अब नष्ट हो चुकी थीं और वे सब क्रॉस के तलहटी में बिखर चुके थे।

यह वेदना कोई सामान्य उदासी का दौर नहीं था, बल्कि यह विश्वास के संकट से जुड़ा एक अवसाद था। इस प्रकार का हतोत्साह भावना की तीव्र आध्यात्मिक पीड़ा की स्थिति है जिसमें संघर्षरत, निराश विश्वास करता महसूस करता है कि वह परमेश्वर द्वारा परित्यक्त है। यह एक निराशाजनक अहसास है कि परमेश्वर की अनुग्रह-सूर्यिमा ग्रहण हो गई है और आत्मा की अँधेरी रात स्थायी रूप से बस गई है।

जबकि हम सभी ऐसे अँधेरे प्रलोभनों का बहादुरी से विरोध करने का प्रयास करते हैं, कई भक्ति-निष्ठ पुरुषों के जीवन में एक संक्षेप निगाह यह दर्शाएगी कि ये प्रलोभन बहुत वास्तविक हैं और मनुष्य के लिए सामान्य भी हैं। ऐसी स्थिति में, जीवन असंभव प्रतीत होता है और हृदय पर छाया ऐसे गहरे अँधेरे की तरह बैठ जाती है कि सुरंग के अंत में कोई प्रकाश नहीं दिखता। क्यों मेरा दुख स्थायी है, और मेरा घाव न भरने वाला है, जो ठीक होना ठुकराता है? क्या तू मुझ पर पूर्णतया झूठा ठहरेगा, और उन जलों के समान जो सूख जाते हैं? —यिर्मयाह 15:18। यह स्पष्ट रूप से एक अतिशयोक्ति है जो विलाप करनेवाले नबी के होंठों से निकल गई, पर यह उसकी आत्मा की गहराइयों में डरी हुई पीड़ा की सीधी झलक देता है।

क्योंकि भाइयो, हम यह न चाहेंगे कि तुम हमारी उस मुश्किल को न जानो जो हमें एशिया में आई, कि हम अत्यन्त दबाए गए, सामर्थ्य से बाहर, यहाँ तक कि जीवन की आशा खो बैठे: परन्तु हममें ही मरने का निर्णय था, कि हम अपने आप पर न भरोसा करें, पर जो मरों को जीवित करता है परमेश्वर पर भरोसा करें —2 कुरिन्थियों 1:8-9। आत्मा की यह अँधेरी रात किसी की पदवी का सम्मान नहीं करती। यह राजाओं और गरीबों, उपदेशकों और पश्चातापियों, सार्वजनिक और निजी लोगों, उपदेशोगृह और बैठक-स्थान—सभी के जीवन में प्रवेश कर लेती है। एम्माुस मार्ग पर ये दो चेलों ने अपनी यात्रा में हर संभव परिदृश्य पर मौखिक रूप से विचार किया था। उन्होंने निस्संदेह दूसरों में खूब दोष भी देखा और व्यक्तिगत खेद भी पाया। “अगर ऐसा हुआ होता तो…” और “काश अगर…” जैसी बातें खूब चर्चा में आईं, पर कुछ भी नतीजे को बदल नहीं सकता था और उनकी बेचैन चिन्ता अभी भी बनी रही।

येरूशलेम से एम्माुस का मार्ग छः हजार फुरलों के लगभग अर्थात लगभग सात मील था। और इस उदास यात्रा पर एक अपरिचित व्यक्ति उस दुखी जोड़े के साथ जुड़ गया और उनसे उनके शोक का कारण पूछ लिया। पर वह कोई जिज्ञासु दर्शक नहीं था। वह उठ चुका प्रभु था जो हमारे अँधेरे पथ पर अपना दिव्य प्रकाश डालने आया है। वह स्वयं को अचानक प्रकट करने के बजाय, और सम्भवतः हमारे लाभ के लिए, धैर्यपूर्वक उन्हें उस सूख चुकी आध्यात्मिक राह का खुलासा करने देता है जिस पर वे चल रहे थे।

इस प्रकार, जैसे जैसे मील के निशान गुज़रते गए, बातचीत खुलती गई, प्रत्येक ने हमारे ईमानदार परन्तु त्रुटिपूर्ण प्रयासों का पर्दाफाश किया जो हमें शांति के नगर से और दूर, आत्मा की अँधेरी रात की ओर ले गए…

…दूसरों की अज्ञानता

और उन में से एक जिसका नाम क्लियोपस था, उसने उत्तर दिया और कहा, क्या तुम ही येरूशलेम के अनजान हो, और यह न जानते कि इन दिनों उसमें क्या-क्या हुआ? —लूका 24:18। न्यूयॉर्क सिटी की सड़कों पर किसी भी अजनबी से पूछिए कि टावरों के गिरने के तीन दिन बाद झंडे आधा-झुके क्यों थे, और आपको वही आश्चर्य भरा उत्तर मिलेगा जो इन दोनों को दिया गया। “तुम इतनी अनजान कैसे हो?” हम सभी उन लोगों पर आश्चर्य करते हैं जो हमारी कल्पना के अनुसार उतनी जानकारी नहीं रखते जितनी हम समझते हैं। आदमी जितना युवा होता है, उतना ही अधिक उत्तर उसे लगता है कि उसकी समझ की भण्डारियों में मौजूद हैं।

यह कुछ नया नहीं है। मूसा, जब युवक थे, तो …सम्झते थे कि उनके भाई समझते होंगे किस प्रकार ईश्वर उनके हाथ द्वारा उन्हें उद्धार देगा: पर वे न समझे —प्रेरितों के काम 7:25। जबकि उन्होंने दृढ़ता से समझ लिया था कि योजना ईश्वर की थी, वे इस बात में भयानक रूप से गलत थे कि वह कितना हिस्सा उनके पास है। यदि हमारा सहारा दिए गए हालात को सुधार नहीं सकता, तो हमारे उत्तर वास्तविक उत्तर नहीं हैं। उनके प्रति स्वाभाविक तिरस्कार जो अलग देखते हैं, वह यह संकेत देता है कि हम गलत पथ पर हैं। जीवन के मीलों पर, मूसा ने उस दर्द की हताशा और उस घड़ी के अँधेरे का अनुभव करना शुरू किया। मैं यह सारा जन अकेला न उठा सकूँगा; क्योंकि यह मेरे लिए बहुत भारी है। और यदि तू मुझसे ऐसा करेगा, तो मुझे मारा दे, मैं तुझसे प्रार्थना करता हूँ, यदि मैंने तेरी दृष्टि में अनुग्रह पाया हो; और मेरे दुरित को मुझसे न दिखा —गिनती 11:14-15। मूसा ने यह पहले जीवन में क्यों नहीं देखा? उसी कारण से कि इन दो भक्त चेलों की आँखें …बँधी हुई थीं कि वे उसे न जानें —लूका 24:16।

…तर्क

और उसने उनसे कहा, किस बात की? और उन्होंने कहा, नाज़रत के यीशु के सम्बन्ध में, जो परमेश्वर और सारे लोगों के सामने कर्म और वचन में एक महान भविष्यवक्ता था —लूका 24:19। उनका मसीह के बारे में अपना निजी धारणात्मक चित्र था, पर वे …एक शीशे के द्वारा, अँधेरे में देखते हैं… —1 कुरिन्थियों 13:12। उनका आंशिक ज्ञान अपनी ही समझ पर अधिक आश्रित था और वे गलत प्रकार के उद्धार की प्रतीक्षा कर रहे थे। उनके लिए, उनका उद्धारकर्ता (भूतकाल में) एक भविष्यवक्ता था जो अब वह नहीं कर सकता था जो वे चाहते थे कि वह करे। हम सभी चाहते हैं कि यीशु हमारे समस्याओं को हल करें और हमें बेहतर महसूस कराएँ, पर उनका उद्देश्य हमें हमारी कल्पनाओं और पाप से मुक्ति दिलाना है।

याकूब के पास हर कारण था कि वह मानें कि बढ़ईपाव और आशीष उसी के होने चाहिए। बसेल में, परमेश्वर ने उसे आशीर्वाद देने का वादा किया था। याकूब ने इसे भौतिक रूप में आने की कल्पना की। और याकूब ने एक प्रतिज्ञा की, कहा, यदि परमेश्वर मेरे साथ होगा, और इस मार्ग में जहाँ मैं जाता हूँ मुझे रखेगा, और मुझे खाने के लिए रोटी तथा पहनने के लिए वस्त्र देगा, ताकि मैं सन्तोषपूर्वक अपने पिता के घर लौट आऊँ; तब यहोवा मेरा परमेश्वर होगा —उत्पत्ति 28:20-21।

परन्तु परमेश्वर की ओर से उसे जो सबसे बड़ा आशीर्वाद मिला, वह गहरी अँधेरी रात के पंखों पर आया। और याकूब अकेला रह गया; और उस पर एक पुरुष ने सुबह के टूटने तक उसे पकड़ लिया। जब उसने देखा कि वह उसके विरुद्ध न जीत पा रहा है, उसने उसके जांघ की जकड़न को छूआ; और याकूब की जांघ की जकड़न लड़ते समय बाहर निकल गई। और उसने कहा, मुझे जाने दे, क्योंकि दिन निकल रहा है। और उसने कहा, मैं तुझको न छोड़ूँगा, जब तक तू मुझे आशीर्वाद न दे। और उसने उससे कहा, तेरा नाम क्या है? और उसने कहा, याकूब। और उसने कहा, तेरा नाम और याकूब न कहा जाएगा, पर इस्राएल कहा जाएगा: क्योंकि तू परमेश्वर और मनुष्यों के साथ एक राजन के समान शक्ति रखेगा, और तू विजय पाया —उत्पत्ति 32:24-28।

याकूब के पास पहले ही भौतिक संपत्ति की प्रचुरता थी। उसे और क्या चाहिए था? याकूब के लिए यह एक अँधेरी रात थी जब उसने पाया कि उसने अपना जीवन भोगों का पीछा करके और परमेश्वर का विरोध करके व्यतीत कर दिया था। अब वह ईश्वरीय चरित्र और आध्यात्मिक समृद्धि चाहता है। उसकी विजय समर्पण के द्वारा हुई, और वह एक मुकुट के साथ एक लंगड़े के रूप में चला गया। भगवान किसी मनुष्य को तब तक पूर्णतया आशीषित नहीं कर सकता जब तक उसने पहले उसके तर्क की शक्तियों पर विजय न पा ली हो।

…दुर्भाग्य

और कैसों ने तथा हमारे प्रधानपुरोहितों ने उसे मृत्यु के लिए सौंप दिया, और उसने उसे क्रूस पर चढ़ाया —लूका 24:20। परमेश्वर विपदाओं को भव्य विजयों में बदलने में निपुण है। फिर भी, मनुष्य अपने चारों ओर देखते हुए अँधकार को कोसता है। हालांकि उसके लिए अच्छी चीजों की बौछार भी हो, …सुबह उनके लिए मृत्यु की छाया के समान है… —यॉब 24:17। हमारे चारों ओर बुराई पर अति जोर देना परमेश्वर की दिव्यता का उपहास है। जबकि हम सभी कभी-कभी उन चीजों पर अफसोस कर सकते हैं जिन्हें हम अलग तरह कर सकते थे, हमें परिणामों को अनिवार्य रूप से परमेश्वर के हाथ में छोड़ देना चाहिए। यॉब ने किसी से कम दुर्भाग्य का अनुभव नहीं किया। इतना अधिक कि उसने …अपने मुँह खोला और अपने दिन को कोसा। और यॉब ने कहा, वह दिन नाश हो जिसमें मैं जन्मा गया था, और वह रात जिसमें कहा गया था, एक पुरुष संतान गर्भ में हुई है। वह दिन अँधेरा हो; परमेश्वर उससे ऊपर न देखे, न प्रकाश उस पर चमके। अँधेरा और मृत्यु की छाया उसे दागे; एक बादल उस पर ठहरे; दिन का अँधेरा उसे भयभीत करे। और उस रात के लिए, अँधेरा उसे धारण करे… —यॉब 3:1-6। पर कहीं पहले कि काले घटनाक्रम सुधरें और उठें, प्रकाश उसकी आत्मा में चमका, और उसने अपने हाथ को अपने मुँह पर रखा और प्रार्थना की और उपासना की।

…व्यक्तिगत हित

पर हम आशा करते थे कि वही था जो इस्राएल को छुड़ाने वाला था… —लूका 24:21। किसी भी विशेष परिस्थिति को समझने का प्रयास करना स्वाभाविक है और इन दोनों ने सही समीकरण चुना था। उनकी भूल उस साधनों के अनुमान में थी जिससे मसीह यह करेंगे और जिस प्रकार का उद्धार वे प्राप्त करने की आशा रखते थे। वे उस दिन की प्रतीक्षा कर रहे थे जब उनकी राष्ट्र रोमनों पर श्रेष्ठ ठहराया जाएगा। जब हम अनजाने में अपनी सुरक्षा की खोज करते हैं, तो वह कटु निराशा की ओर ले जाती है। नाओं ने सोचा …वह निश्‍चित तौर पर मेरे पास आएगा, खड़ा होगा, और प्रभु अपने परमेश्वर के नाम का उच्चारण करेगा, और अपने हाथ से जगह पर प्रहार करेगा, और कुष्ठरोगी को ठीक करेगा —2 राजा 5:11।

अब्राहम को कना न की भूमि का वचन मिला और उसने पुष्टि के लिए कहा। तब उसने परमेश्वर द्वारा निर्देशित वाचा-बलिदान तैयार किया, पर पूरा दिन बीत गया और परमेश्वर ने उनके साथ कुछ नहीं किया। और जब सूर्य ढल रहा था, अब्राम पर गहरी नींद छा गई; और देखो, उस पर घोर अँधेरे की भीषण भयावहता चढ़ गई —उत्पत्ति 15:12।

जब अब्राहम ने प्रभु से अपनी offering प्राप्त करने की प्रतीक्षा की, वह शिकार करने वाले पक्षियों को दौड़ता रहा। पर जैसे-जैसे दिन समाप्ति के निकट आया, उसने स्वयं को परमेश्वर द्वारा परित्यक्त महसूस किया और अँधेरी रात उसकी आत्मा पर उतरने लगी। हमें सितारों को देखने और उसकी आवाज सुनने के लिए चीजों के अँधेरे होने तक मध्यरात्रि के अनुभव की आवश्यकता होती है। परन्तु हममें ही मरने का निर्णय था, कि हम अपने आप पर न भरोसा करें, पर जो मरों को जीवित करता है परमेश्वर पर भरोसा करें —2 कुरिन्थियों 1:9।

…अधीरता

…और इसके बावजूद, आज तीसरा दिन है जब से ये बातें हुईं —लूका 24:21। हम में से कई इतने अनुशासित हैं कि एक समय तक प्रतीक्षा कर सकें। यह तब होता है जब हमारी आशा टाली जाती है (देखें नीतिवचन 13:12) कि हमारे हृदय रोगी और कमज़ोर हो जाते हैं। इन दो के लिए तीन दिन लंबा समय जैसा लगा। पर तीन दिन, सप्ताह, महीने, वर्ष, या दशकों तक सब कुछ परमेश्वर की घड़ी के अधीन है। कितने दिनों तक तू मुझे भूल जाएगा, हे यहोवा? सदा? कितने दिनों तक तू मुझसे अपना मुख छिपायेगा? —भजन संहिता 13:1।

यूसुफ ने अपने भाइयों और पोटीफर के बदसलूकी को धैर्यपूर्वक सहा, पर कालकोठरी लंबी हो गयी, और उसने शराबकर्मी से प्रार्थना की कि जब वह फिर से प्रतिष्ठित होगा तब उसे याद दिला दे। पर यह दो पूर्ण वर्ष (उत्पत्ति 41:1) था जब तक फिरफ़िरौन ने सपना देखा और यूसुफ को बुलाया गया। पर यह शराबकर्मी की भूल न थी जितना कि परमेश्वर की इच्छा थी जिसने यूसुफ को …लोह में पड़ा दिया गया: जब तक कि उसका वचन न आया: यहोवा का वचन ने उसे आज़माया — भजन संहिता 105:18-19। अँधकार के अनुशासन से धैर्य सीखने के लिए इससे अधिक प्रभावी मार्ग नहीं है, जिससे कुछ ही संत छूटते हैं।

…स्वयं-दयालुता

हाँ, और हमारे साथ की कुछ औरतें भी थी जो सुबह-सुबह कब्र पर आईं; और जब उन्होंने उसका शरीर न पाया, वे आकर कहने लगीं कि उन्होंने भी स्वर्गदूत का दर्शन किया, जिन्होंने कहा कि वह जीवित है —लूका 24:22-23। कोई भी यह खोने का एहसास पसंद नहीं करता। वास्तव में, मनोविज्ञान ने एक नई विकृति खोजी है—FOMO (कुछ चूक जाने का डर)। महिलाओं द्वारा लाई खबर अच्छी थी और आश्चर्यजनक मोड़ था, फिर भी यह दूसरों के लिए कोई आनन्द नहीं लाया क्योंकि यह उनके साथ नहीं हुआ था। अच्छा समाचार आत्म-दया में डूबे व्यक्ति में मुश्किल से ही प्रवेश कर पाता है और ईलिया ऐसा ही था। उसकी अँधेरी रात कार्मेल पर्वत पर बैल के नबियों के विरुद्ध एक शानदार जीत की प्राप्ति के बाद आई। पर अपनी आंतरिक भावनाओं के अँधेरे में …उसने अपने लिए प्रार्थना की कि वह मर सके; और कहा, बहुत हुआ; अब, हे यहोवा, मेरा जीवन ले ले; क्योंकि मैं अपने पिता से भी अच्छा नहीं हूँ —1 राजा 19:4।

…विफलता के भाव

और हमारे साथ के कुछ लोग कब्र पर गए, और जैसा कि औरतों ने कहा वैसा ही पाया: पर उसे वे न देखे —लूका 24:24। यह सोचना आसान है, “उनके लिए यह सफल रहा पर मेरे लिए नहीं।” जबकि असफल प्रयास हमें हतोत्साहित कर सकते हैं, यह जरूरी नहीं कि हमारी तरफ से कोई असफलता हो। यूहन्ना बपतिस्मा देनेवाले ने जनता को पश्चाताप के लिए सच्चाई से बुलाया, मसीह को बपतिस्मा दिया, और स्वर्ग से गरजती हुई आवाज़ का साक्षी बना। उसने ठीक से आने वाले मसीह की घोषणा की और अपने चेलों की ओर संकेत किया …परमेश्वर का मेमना, जो संसार के पाप को हटाता है —यूहन्ना 1:29। इस सेवा ने उसे एक अँधेरी कारागार कोठरी में एक सुरक्षित स्थान दिलाया। वह असुविधा और तुच्छ आहार का अच्छी तरह आदी था, पर परमेश्वर द्वारा पूर्णतया परित्याग का अनुभव ही उसे गहरे संदेहों तक ले गया। और यूहन्ना ने अपने चेलों में से दो को बुलाकर उन्हें यीशु के पास भेजा, कह कर, क्या तू वही है जो आना चाहिए? या हम किसी और की तलाश करें? —लूका 7:19।

“क्या मैं गलत था?” अँधेरे में उसने एक प्रश्न-चिह्न की ढलान पर जीवन जीना शुरू कर दिया। जॉन बनयन इसे ‘दु:ख का दलदल’ कहते हैं। यह ईसाई के लिए D-Day जैसा प्रतीत हो सकता है, पर हमारी असफल प्रयत्नों पर अनावश्यक जोर पुनरुत्थान को बढ़ावा नहीं देता।

निष्कर्ष

सारी आध्यात्मिक अँधेरियाँ पूरी तरह से टालने योग्य नहीं हैं। हर आध्यात्मिक अनुभव दिल से आशीर्वाद का समय नहीं होता, न ही हर स्थान ऐसा ही। वे समय आते हैं जब सत्कार और परिक्षाएँ संतों को आत्मिक हिसाब-किताब की ओर लाने के लिए निर्धारित की जाती हैं, जिन्हें केवल अँधेरी रातें ही उपलब्ध करा सकती हैं। स्वयं यीशु को भी हमारे समान प्रकार की परीक्षा से गुज़रना पड़ा, जब क्रूस पर नवें घंटे के व्याप्त अँधेरे में, उसकी आवाज़ गूँजी …बड़ी आवाज़ के साथ कह रहा था, एली, एली, लम माय सबक्तानि? अर्थात, मेरे परमेश्वर, मेरे परमेश्वर, तूने मुझे क्यों परित्यक्त किया? —मत्ती 27:46।

एम्माुस का मार्ग इस सत्य का साक्षी है कि विश्वास का जीवंत अस्तित्व आध्यात्मिक अवसाद की गैरमौजूदगी की गारंटी नहीं देता। यह वास्तविक लोगों की कहानी है जिनके वास्तविक विश्वास ने वास्तविक परीक्षाओं का सामना किया। यह हमें सिखाने में मदद करता है कि यहां तक कि आध्यात्मिक सुखों को भी बहुत दृढ़ता से नही पकड़े रखना चाहिए। हमारे निकट और दूर-दराज के भविष्य के आश्वस्त दृष्टिकोणों को विनम्रता की आग में डुबोना चाहिए। अँधेरी रात वह स्थान है जहाँ आत्म-प्रमोचन मरता है, और परमेश्वर का गहन ज्ञान जन्म लेता है। यह हमें उन आशीषों के प्रेम से स्थानान्तरण कर देता है जो वह देता है, उस प्रेम की ओर जो उसके साथ हमारे सम्बन्ध और उससे मिलने वाली संगति के लिए है।

क्लियोपस के यात्रासाथी का नाम कभी नहीं बताया गया। कुछ लोग सोचते हैं कि वह उसकी पत्नी थी। कुछ का दावा है कि वह लूका था। पर उनकी पहचान छोड़ी गयी, शायद ताकि हम अधिक प्रवृत्त हों कि उस रिक्त स्थान में अपना स्वयं का नाम भर सकें। येरूशलेम से सात मील पर हम उद्धारकर्ता वास्तव में कौन है इस कठोर वास्तविकता पर ठोकर खाते हैं और यह कि मुक्ति केवल उसकी मिल्कियत चिन्हित करने वाला मुहर नहीं है। हमारी आँखों से पर्दा हट जाता है और आत्मा की अँधेरी रात परमेश्वर की उपस्थिति की दोपहरी उजियाली के सामने हट जाती है। तब हम प्रसन्नता से शान्ति के नगर की ओर भागते हैं, केवल फिर से गलत समझे जाने के लिए। और वे गए और शेष लोगों को कहा: पर वे उन पर विश्वास न किए —मरकुस 16:13।

और इसलिए, मैं ऐसे विचार लिखने की भी उपयोगिता पर आश्चर्य करता हूँ। यह कोई ऐसा अनुभव नहीं है जिसे बनाया जा सके और बौद्धिक रूप से समझा जा सके। यह परमेश्वर के साथ बहुत व्यक्तिगत समागम है और प्रत्येक व्यक्ति के लिए विशिष्ट रूप से तैयार किया गया है। पर शायद हम, अपनी उथली पीढ़ी में, अँधेरे से घृणा के साथ मिलने के बदले उसे अपनाने के लिए प्रोत्साहित हो सकें। और वहीं, रात की भयावह अंधकार में, प्रकाश के उद्धारकर्ता को अपनाना सीखें।

दीर्घकाल तक मेरी कैदी आत्मा पड़ी रही,
पाप और स्वभाव की रात में कस कर बँधी हुई।
तेरी दृष्टि ने जीवनदान की एक किरण फैलाई,
मैं जाग उठा; क़ैदखाना प्रकाश से जल उठा।
मेरी जलियाँ ढीली पड़ गईं। मेरा हृदय मुक्त हुआ।
मैं उठा, निकला, और तेरा अनुसरण किया।

- चार्ल्स वेज़ले

Greetings of love in the blessed name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. Many Christians have gone through a time of trial and testing during the past several years, yet we trust that each one is able to say with Paul… Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content –Philippians 4:11.

Summer is hard upon us, along with the heat and humidity that goes along with summers here in Ohio. Springtime, along with the normal planting season, was extra long and drawn out. But, by now, most of what is known locally as “the spring work” has been finished. The farmers’ crops and the gardeners’ herbs are pushing through the cool soil and towards the heat and light of the sun.

In this issue you can take a stroll on the road to Emmaus and try to put yourself in the sandals of Jesus’ disciples as they puzzled over the sudden turn of events surrounding Christ’s death, burial, and alleged “resurrection”. You can try to picture yourself with Daniel of old as he chose to keep praying like normal at his open window, while knowing full well that this simple act most likely could change his life forever. You can marvel with little “Ellie” how God met the “desires of her heart” even before she knew things weren’t working out according to plan.

Something new in this issue is the beginning of a series by Brother Donald Brechbill on “discipleship”. Disciple has almost the same spelling as discipline. For many, discipline carries a negative connotation, which hopefully will not interfere with the reader being drawn to what Brother Donald has to share. Let’s remember that Jesus gave personal example of the discipleship model—He chose and called “disciples” to follow and learn from Him. Later He sent them out two by two to teach and make more disciples. And then when He gave the “Great Commission” it was to His disciples at that time, and to all future disciples—the Church of Jesus Christ. We trust that each one can be inspired by this series.

Coming up in future issues, we are planning to have a “Song of the Quarter” and a section on various aspects of “Church History”. You can pray for us as we continue to move forward with our ministry and our magazine.

Just a friendly reminder… We encourage feedback from our readers. If you have been especially blessed by a certain article, feedback is helpful for us as a board, and it is encouraging for our writers. Also, if there is something specific that someone wishes to see included in future magazine issues, we welcome the input. This helps provide ideas for us as a board when choosing articles and when asking authors to write.

In the spring of 2022, we made some changes with our ministry in our endeavors to keep the work of The Berean Voice moving forward into the future. Personnel changes:

Brother Andrew (our designer) has become increasingly busy as a young father with a growing family and as a deacon for our local church congregation. In looking at this challenge, the board decided to support Andrew’s desire to find someone to help him (for now) with the bulk of the design work for each issue of our magazine—The Heartbeat of the Remnant. Thus, there may be some slight changes in the “style” of design in upcoming issues.

In the spring of 2022, there was a decision to seek several new board members to replace several others who had quit over the last number of years due to personal responsibilities. After praying for the Lord’s wisdom and direction, and after consultation with the leadership of our church, Brother Joe Mast and Brother Sheldon Bower were chosen to fill the empty slots on the board. These brothers have both graciously accepted this calling and are already allowing God to use their spiritual gifts to make a difference

Brother Joe Tindall has been a board member for The Berean Voice since our beginning in June of 2016. Due to his age (83) Brother Joe asked to be relieved of his duties as a board member. At our monthly board meeting in May of 2022, the board honored Brother Joe’s request. We will miss the stability of his quiet wisdom in our board meetings and during our article selection process. Please join us in prayer for Brother Joe and his family as he and his wife face the end of their lives and all that goes along with that season of life—that they might remain faithful and courageous.

May God bless and keep each one.

Curvin L Wenger

Grüße der Liebe im gesegneten Namen unseres Herrn und Erlösers Jesus Christus. Viele Christen haben in den vergangenen Jahren eine Zeit der Prüfung und Erprobung durchgemacht, doch vertrauen wir darauf, dass jeder mit Paulus sagen kann… Nicht, dass ich des Mangels halber rede; denn ich habe gelernt, in welchem Zustand ich auch bin, darin zufrieden zu sein –Philipper 4:11.

Der Sommer steht vor der Tür, zusammen mit der Hitze und Feuchtigkeit, die die Sommer hier in Ohio mit sich bringen. Der Frühling, zusammen mit der normalen Pflanzzeit, war besonders lang und zog sich hin. Aber inzwischen ist das, was hier örtlich als „Frühjahrsarbeit“ bekannt ist, größtenteils erledigt. Die Felder der Bauern und die Kräuter der Gärtner drängen durch die kühle Erde und hinauf zur Hitze und zum Licht der Sonne.

In dieser Ausgabe können Sie einen Spaziergang auf dem Weg nach Emmaus machen und versuchen, sich in die Sandalen der Jünger Jesu zu versetzen, während sie über die plötzliche Wendung der Ereignisse um Christi Tod, Begräbnis und angebliche „Auferstehung“ rätseln. Sie können sich vorstellen, wie Sie mit dem alten Daniel beten wie gewohnt an seinem offenen Fenster, obwohl Sie ganz genau wissen, dass diese einfache Tat sein Leben für immer verändern könnte. Sie können mit der kleinen „Ellie“ staunen, wie Gott die „Wünsche ihres Herzens“ erfüllte, noch ehe sie wusste, dass die Dinge nicht nach Plan liefen.

Neu in dieser Ausgabe ist der Beginn einer Serie von Bruder Donald Brechbill über „Jüngerschaft“. Das Wort Jünger hat fast die gleiche Schreibweise wie Disziplin. Für viele hat Disziplin eine negative Konnotation, was hoffentlich nicht verhindert, dass der Leser von dem angezogen wird, was Bruder Donald zu teilen hat. Lasst uns daran denken, dass Jesus ein persönliches Beispiel des Jüngerschaftsmodells gab—Er wählte und rief „Jünger“, damit sie Ihm folgen und von Ihm lernen. Später sandte Er sie paarweise aus, um zu lehren und mehr Jünger zu machen. Und als Er den „Großen Auftrag“ gab, richtete er sich an Seine Jünger zu jener Zeit und an alle zukünftigen Jünger—die Kirche Jesu Christi. Wir vertrauen darauf, dass jeder durch diese Serie inspiriert werden kann.

In zukünftigen Ausgaben planen wir, ein „Lied des Quartals“ und eine Rubrik zu verschiedenen Aspekten der „Kirchengeschichte“ zu haben. Sie können für uns beten, während wir mit unserem Dienst und unserer Zeitschrift weiter voranschreiten.

Nur eine freundliche Erinnerung… Wir begrüßen Rückmeldungen von unseren Lesern. Wenn Sie durch einen bestimmten Artikel besonders gesegnet wurden, sind Rückmeldungen für uns als Vorstand hilfreich und ermutigend für unsere Autoren. Auch wenn jemand etwas Spezielles in zukünftigen Ausgaben der Zeitschrift sehen möchte, freuen wir uns über Hinweise. Das hilft uns als Vorstand bei der Auswahl von Artikeln und bei der Aufforderung an Autoren zu schreiben.

Im Frühjahr 2022 haben wir einige Änderungen in unserem Dienst vorgenommen, um die Arbeit The Berean Voice weiter in die Zukunft zu tragen. Personalveränderungen:

Bruder Andrew (unser Gestalter) ist als junger Vater mit wachsender Familie und als Diakon unserer örtlichen Kirchengemeinde immer stärker eingespannt. Angesichts dieser Herausforderung beschloss der Vorstand, Andrews Wunsch zu unterstützen, vorübergehend jemanden zu finden, der ihm den Großteil der Gestaltungsarbeit für jede Ausgabe unserer Zeitschrift—The Heartbeat of the Remnant—abnimmt. Daher kann es in künftigen Ausgaben zu kleinen Änderungen im „Stil“ des Designs kommen.

Im Frühjahr 2022 wurde die Entscheidung getroffen, mehrere neue Vorstandsmitglieder zu suchen, um einige andere zu ersetzen, die in den letzten Jahren aus persönlichen Gründen ausgeschieden waren. Nach Gebet um Gottes Weisheit und Leitung und nach Rücksprache mit der Leitung unserer Kirche wurden Bruder Joe Mast und Bruder Sheldon Bower ausgewählt, die freien Plätze im Vorstand zu besetzen. Diese Brüder haben diese Berufung beide gnädig angenommen und lassen Gott bereits ihre geistlichen Gaben einsetzen, um einen Unterschied zu machen.

Bruder Joe Tindall war seit unserem Beginn im Juni 2016 Mitglied des Vorstands von The Berean Voice. Aufgrund seines Alters (83) bat Bruder Joe darum, von seinen Aufgaben als Vorstandsmitglied entbunden zu werden. Auf unserer monatlichen Vorstandssitzung im Mai 2022 kam dem Wunsch von Bruder Joe entsprochen. Wir werden die Beständigkeit seiner stillen Weisheit in unseren Vorstandssitzungen und während unseres Auswahlverfahrens für Artikel vermissen. Bitte betet mit uns für Bruder Joe und seine Familie, während er und seine Frau dem Ende ihres Lebens und allem, was mit dieser Lebensphase einhergeht, entgegensehen—dass sie treu und mutig bleiben mögen.

Gott segne und behüte jeden Einzelnen.

Curvin L Wenger

And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these
that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? –Luke 24:17.

On June 6, 1944, 156,000 American, British, and Canadian troops landed on a 50-mile stretch of beach in Normandy, France. After several months of intense fighting, they overcame the initial defenses and swarmed into the German-held territory. The surprise attack, known as D-Day, caught the Germans off guard. However, it wasn’t until March of the next year that France was finally liberated from German forces. D-day was the beginning of the end of World War II on the western front and it was the event that seemed to sap the life from the notorious German army, from which they never recovered. It appears rather coincidental that so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.

I can imagine that these two believers, plodding upon the road to Emmaus that dim and dismal evening, were feeling a little the same way. Their D-Day had arrived totally unexpected. I would suspect that every living person has at one time or another experienced moments of intense sadness—their own D-day, so-to-speak. Even some animals have been known to express a melancholy mood at the death of their master or mate. But these two disciples seemed to be experiencing a pain far beyond the normal loss of a friend. They were staring into the face of the grim reality that all their bright hopes of a shining tomorrow were hopelessly shattered in a ruinous heap at the foot of the cross.

This agony was no ordinary fit of depression but rather it was a depression linked to a crisis of faith. This type of discouragement is a state of intense spiritual anguish in which the struggling, despairing believer feels he is abandoned by God. It is a hopeless feeling that the sun of God's blessedness has been eclipsed and the dark night of the soul has become a permanent resident within.

While all of us seek to valiantly resist such dark temptations, a brief search into the lives of many godly men will reveal that these temptations are very real and are quite common to man. In such a condition, life seems impossible and the impending gloom that has settled upon the heart sees no light at the end of the tunnel. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed? wilt thou be altogether unto me as a liar, and as waters that fail? –Jeremiah 15:18. This is obviously an overstated exaggeration that escaped the lips of the weeping prophet, but it gives us a direct snapshot into the dreaded pain in the depths of his soul.

For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:8-9. This dark night of the soul shows no respect to persons. It invades the lives of princes and paupers, preachers and penitents, public and private people, pulpits and pews. These two disciples had verbally revisited every possible scenario in their journey along the Emmaus Road. They had no doubt found plenty of fault in others as well as personal regret. The “what ifs” and “if onlys” had thoroughly been discussed, but nothing could reverse the outcome and their restless anxiety lingered still.

The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs or approximately seven miles. And along this doleful journey a Stranger joined ranks with the distraught duo in their D-Day and asked them for an account of their sadness. But he is no curious onlooker. He is the risen Lord who has come to cast His heavenly light upon our darkened pathway. Rather than revealing Himself abruptly, and perhaps for our benefit, he patiently allows them to expose the depleted spiritual road that they were treading upon.

Thus, the conversation unfolds as the mile markers pass, each revealing our sincere erroneous efforts that lead us further from the city of peace and into the dark night of the soul…

…The Ignorance of Others

And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? –Luke 24:18. Ask any stranger on the streets of New York City why the flags were flying at half-mast three days after the towers fell on September 11, and you would receive the same incredulous answer ascribed to these two. “How can you be so ignorant?” We all tend to marvel at people who do not hold the same knowledge that we imagine ourselves to possess. The younger the man, the more answers that he believes the coffers of his understanding hold.

This is nothing new. Moses, as a young man, …supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not –Acts 7:25. While he firmly understood that he owned the plan of God, he was badly mistaken in the percentage that he possessed. If our recourse cannot rectify the given situation, our answers are not the real answer. The heartfelt disdain that naturally arises toward those who see it differently is the beginning marker that we are on the wrong path. Miles down the pathway of life, Moses began to feel the desperation of that pain and the darkness of the hour. I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me. And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness –Numbers 11:14-15. Why did Moses not see this earlier in life? For the same cause that these two fervent disciples’ …eyes were holden that they should not know him –Luke 24:16.

…Reason

And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people –Luke 24:19. They had their private perception of who the Christ was, but they were seeing …through a glass, darkly… –1 Corinthians 13:12. Their partial knowledge was leaning heavily on their own understanding and looking for the wrong kind of redemption. To them, their redeemer was (past tense) a prophet that no longer could do what they wanted him to do. We all want Jesus to solve our problems and make us feel better, but His purpose is to free us from our presumption and sin.

Jacob had every reason to believe that the birthright and blessing was to be his. At Bethel, God had promised to bless him. Jacob reckoned this to arrive in a material format. And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God –Genesis 28:20-21.

But the greatest blessing he ever received from God arrived to him on the wings of a deep dark night. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him. And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed –Genesis 32:24-28.

Jacob had already accumulated an abundance of earthly possessions. What more could he want? It was a dark night for Jacob when he discovered that he’d spent his life pursuing possessions and resisting God. He now seeks godly character and spiritual affluence. His victory was through surrender, and he limped away as a cripple with a crown. The Lord cannot fully bless a man until He has first conquered his powers of reason.

…Ill Fate

And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him –Luke 24:20. God specializes in turning grave dilemmas into monumental victories. Still, man looks around him and curses the darkness about him. Though there may be a volley of good reciprocating them, …the morning is to them even as the shadow of death… –Job 24:17. To give undo emphasis upon the evil about us is to mock the divinity of God. While we all may regret at times things that we could have done or said differently, we must invariably leave the results in the hands of God. Job experienced as much ill fate as anybody. So much so that he opened …his mouth, and cursed his day. And Job spake, and said, Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived. Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it. Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. As for that night, let darkness seize upon it… –Job 3:1-6. But somewhere before the dark events were rectified and lifted, the light shined into his soul, and he laid his hand to his mouth and worshiped.

…Personal Agenda

But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel… –Luke 24:21. It is but natural to attempt to understand any given situation and these two had selected the correct equation. Their folly lay in the presumption of the means that Christ was to perform this and the type of redemption they were to receive. They were looking forward to the day when their nation would be exalted over the Romans. When we unwittingly seek our own security, it is bound to lead to bitter disappointment. Naaman thought …He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper –2 Kings 5:11.

Abraham was promised the land of Canaan and he asked for a confirmation. He then prepared the covenant sacrifice prescribed by God, but the entire day passed, and God did nothing with them. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. –Genesis 15:12.

As Abraham waited on God to receive his offering, he continued to beat back the birds of prey. But as the day neared an end he began to feel abandoned by God and the dark night began to settle upon his soul. It takes a midnight experience for things to get dark enough for us to see the stars and quiet enough to hear His voice. But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:9.

…Impatience

…And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done –Luke 24:21. Many of us are disciplined enough to hold out for a season. It is when our hope is deferred (see Proverbs 13:12) that our hearts grow sick and faint. Three days seemed like a long time to these two. But three days, weeks, months, years, or even decades are all within the disposal of God’s clock. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? –Psalm 13:1.

Joseph patiently endured the ill treatment of his brothers and Potiphar, but the dungeon got long, and he entreated the butler to send for him when he was restored his position. But it was two full years (Genesis 41:1) until Pharoah dreamed and Joseph was finally hailed forth. But it was not so much the fault of the butler as it was the will of God who had called Joseph to be …laid in iron: Until the time that his word came: the word of the LORD tried him –Psalm 105:18-19. There is no more effective avenue to teach us patience than the discipline of darkness, from which few saints are exempt.

…Self-Pity

Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre; And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive –Luke 24:22-23. No one enjoys missing out. In fact, psychology has uncovered a new disorder –FOMO (fear of missing out). The tidings brought by the women was good news and an amazing turn of events, yet it brought the others no joy for it did not happen to them. Good news can rarely penetrate a person immersed in self-pity and Elijah was one such. His dark night arrived on the heels of a breathtaking triumph on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal. But in the blackness of his own inner feelings …he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers –1 Kings 19:4.

…Feelings of Failure

And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not –Luke 24:24. It is easy to think, “It worked for them but it’s not working for me.” While unsuccessful efforts may discourage us, it is not necessarily a failure on our part. John the Baptist had faithfully called the people to repentance, baptized Christ, and witnessed the thundering voice from heaven. He accurately announced the coming Messiah and pointed his disciples to …the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world –John 1:29. This ministry earned him a secure place in a dark prison cell. He had been well accustomed to the lack of comfort and a meager diet, but it was the feelings of utter abandonment by God that brought him unto dark doubts. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? –Luke 7:19.

“Was I wrong?” In the darkness he began to experience life on the sloping back of a question mark. John Bunyan describes it as the slough of despond. It may appear like D-Day for the Christian, but undue emphasis upon our unsuccessful efforts promotes no resurrection.

Conclusion

Not all spiritual darkness is completely avoidable. Not every spiritual experience is a time of heartfelt blessing, nor is every place. There are times of persecution and testing that are designed to bring saints unto the soul reckoning that only dark nights can minister unto. Jesus Himself was tempted in a similar manner to us, when in the pervading darkness of the ninth hour on the cross, His voice rang out …with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? –Matthew 27:46.

The road to Emmaus bears witness to the fact that a vibrant existence of faith gives no guarantee of the absence of spiritual depression. It is a story about real people with real faith experiencing real trials. It is helpful to teach us that even spiritual pleasures ought not to be held too tightly. Our confident visions for the future both immediate and long term must be immersed in the fires of humility. The dark night is the place where such self-deception dies, and an intimate knowledge of God is birthed. It transitions us from loving God for the blessings He gives us, to loving God for our relationship with Him and the communion that follows.

The traveling companion of Cleopas was never mentioned. Some think it was his wife. Some claim it was Luke. But their identity was omitted, perhaps so that we might be more apt to fill the vacancy with our own name. Seven miles from Jerusalem we stumble upon the stark reality of whom the Savior really is and that salvation is more than just a rubber stamp marking His possession. The scales fall from our eyes and the dark night of the soul gives way to the brightness of the noonday light of the presence of God. It is then that we make our joyous dash back to the city of peace only to be misunderstood again. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them –Mark 16:13.

And so, I wonder even at the profitability of writing down such thoughts. It is not an encounter that can be manufactured and intellectually understood. It is a highly personal convocation with God and tailored specifically to each individual. But perhaps we, in our shallow generation, can be encouraged to reach out and embrace the darkness instead of meeting it with a loathing resistance. And there in the menacing darkness of night, learn to embrace the Savior of light.

Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature's night.
Thine eye diffused a quickening ray,
I woke; the dungeon flamed with light.
My chains fell off. My heart was free.
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

- Charles Wesley

E disse-lhes ele: Que comunicações são estas entre vós, andando e entristecendo-vos?
–Lucas 24:17.

Em 6 de junho de 1944, 156.000 tropas americanas, britânicas e canadenses desembarcaram numa extensão de praia de 50 milhas na Normandia, França. Depois de vários meses de combates intensos, elas superaram as defesas iniciais e inundaram o território ocupado pelos alemães. O ataque surpresa, conhecido como Dia D, pegou os alemães desprevenidos. Entretanto, só em março do ano seguinte a França foi finalmente libertada das forças alemãs. O Dia D foi o começo do fim da Segunda Guerra Mundial na frente ocidental e foi o evento que pareceu sugar a vida do notório exército alemão, do qual nunca mais se recuperaram. Parece bastante coincidente que tantas palavras com conotação negativa comecem com a letra D: Decepção, Dúvida, Doloroso, Desgraça, Desilusão, Desânimo, Sombrio, Derrota, Desalento, Depressão, Desespero, Devastação, Decepção e Morte.

Consigo imaginar que esses dois crentes, caminhando pela estrada para Emaús naquela tarde sombria e melancólica, sentiam-se um pouco da mesma maneira. O Dia D deles havia chegado totalmente inesperado. Suspeito que toda pessoa viva tenha, em algum momento, experimentado momentos de tristeza intensa — seu próprio Dia D, por assim dizer. Até alguns animais já foram conhecidos por expressar um humor melancólico na morte de seu dono ou parceiro. Mas esses dois discípulos pareciam estar experimentando uma dor bem além da perda normal de um amigo. Eles encaravam a realidade sombria de que todas as suas brilhantes esperanças de um amanhã radiante estavam irremediavelmente despedaçadas em um monte arruinado aos pés da cruz.

Essa agonia não era um ataque ordinário de depressão, mas sim uma depressão ligada a uma crise de fé. Esse tipo de desencorajamento é um estado de angústia espiritual intensa no qual o crente em luta e em desespero sente-se abandonado por Deus. É uma sensação de desesperança de que o sol da bem-aventurança de Deus foi eclipsado e a noite escura da alma tornou-se residente permanente no interior.

Enquanto todos nós buscamos resistir valentemente a tais tentações sombrias, uma breve busca nas vidas de muitos homens piedosos revelará que essas tentações são muito reais e bastante comuns ao homem. Nessa condição, a vida parece impossível e o negrume iminente que se instalou sobre o coração não vê luz no fim do túnel. Por que a minha dor é perpétua, e a minha ferida dura sem remédio, que se recusam a sarar? Porventura tu serás totalmente para mim como um mentiroso e como águas que se conturbam? –Jeremias 15:18. Isso é obviamente uma hipérbole exagerada que escapou aos lábios do profeta choroso, mas nos dá um instantâneo direto da terrível dor nas profundezas de sua alma.

Porque não queremos, irmãos, que ignoreis a tribulação que nos sobreveio na Ásia; que excedeu as nossas forças, de modo que até a própria vida desesperávamos; –2 Coríntios 1:8-9. Essa noite escura da alma não respeita pessoas. Invade a vida de príncipes e pobres, pregadores e penitentes, pessoas públicas e privadas, púlpitos e bancos. Esses dois discípulos haviam revisitado verbalmente cada possível cenário em sua jornada pela estrada de Emaús. Sem dúvida encontraram muitas falhas nos outros, bem como arrependimento pessoal. O “e se” e o “se ao menos” foram exaustivamente discutidos, mas nada poderia reverter o resultado e sua ansiedade inquieta persistia.

A estrada de Jerusalém a Emaús tinha cerca de sessenta estádios ou aproximadamente sete milhas. E ao longo dessa jornada dolorosa um Estranho juntou-se ao duo angustiado em seu Dia D e lhes perguntou a razão da sua tristeza. Mas ele não é um espectador curioso. Ele é o Senhor ressuscitado que veio lançar Sua luz celestial sobre nosso caminho escurecido. Em vez de se revelar de forma abrupta, e talvez para nosso benefício, ele pacientemente permite que eles exponham a estrada espiritual esvaziada sobre a qual caminhavam.

Assim, a conversa se desenrola à medida que os marcos do caminho passam, cada um revelando nossos sinceros esforços errôneos que nos conduzem mais longe da cidade da paz e para a noite escura da alma…

…A Ignorância dos Outros

E um deles, chamado Cleopas, respondeu-lhe: És tu, pois, o único morador em Jerusalém, e não sabes as coisas que ali se passaram nestes dias? –Lucas 24:18. Pergunte a qualquer estranho nas ruas de Nova York por que as bandeiras estavam a meio mastro três dias depois da queda das torres em 11 de setembro, e você receberá a mesma resposta incrédula atribuída a estes dois. “Como podes ser tão ignorante?” Todos nós tendemos a nos espantar com pessoas que não têm o mesmo conhecimento que imaginamos possuir. Quanto mais jovem o homem, mais respostas ele acredita que os cofres de sua compreensão contêm.

Isso não é novidade. Moisés, quando jovem, …pensou que seus irmãos haviam compreendido que Deus por sua mão lhes daria a salvação; mas não entenderam –Atos 7:25. Embora ele entendesse firmemente que possuía o plano de Deus, estava profundamente enganado quanto à porcentagem que realmente possuía. Se nosso recurso não pode retificar a situação dada, nossas respostas não são a resposta real. O desdém sincero que naturalmente surge em direção àqueles que veem de modo diferente é o marcador inicial de que estamos no caminho errado. Quilômetros adiante na trajetória da vida, Moisés começou a sentir o desespero daquela dor e a escuridão da hora. Eu não posso suportar todo este povo, por ser para mim demasiado pesado. Se comigo agires assim, mata-me, peço-te, de uma vez, se tenho achado graça aos teus olhos; e não me faças ver a minha miséria –Números 11:14-15. Por que Moisés não viu isso mais cedo? Pelo mesmo motivo que os olhos desses dois fervorosos discípulos …foram impedidos de o conhecer –Lucas 24:16.

…Razão

Então lhes disse ele: Que coisas? E responderam-lhe: De Jesus de Nazaré, que foi homem profeta poderoso em obras e palavras diante de Deus e de todo o povo –Lucas 24:19. Eles tinham sua percepção particular de quem era o Cristo, mas viam …por um espelho, em enigma… –1 Coríntios 13:12. Seu conhecimento parcial apoiava-se fortemente em sua própria compreensão e procurava o tipo errado de redenção. Para eles, seu redentor era (no pretérito) um profeta que já não podia fazer o que eles queriam que ele fizesse. Todos queremos que Jesus resolva nossos problemas e nos faça sentir melhor, mas Seu propósito é nos libertar de nossa presunção e do pecado.

Jacó tinha toda a razão para crer que a primogenitura e a bênção lhe pertenciam. Em Betel, Deus havia prometido abençoá-lo. Jacó supôs que isso ocorreria em forma material. E Jacó fez um voto, dizendo: Se Deus for comigo, e me guardar neste caminho que eu for, e me der pão para comer e roupa para vestir, de modo que eu torne à casa de meu pai em paz, então o SENHOR será o meu Deus –Gênesis 28:20-21.

Mas a maior bênção que ele jamais recebeu de Deus chegou-lhe nas asas de uma noite profunda e escura. E Jacó ficou só; e lutou com ele um varão até a alva. E quando viu que não prevalecia contra ele, tocou na articulação da sua coxa; e a articulação da coxa de Jacó saiu do seu sítio, enquanto lutava com ele. E disse: Deixa-me ir, porque a alva já se aproxima. E disse: Não te deixarei, senão que me abençoes. E disse-lhe: Qual é o teu nome? E ele disse: Jacó. E disse: Não se chamará mais o teu nome Jacó, mas Israel; porque como príncipe lutaste com Deus e com os homens e prevaleceste –Gênesis 32:24-28.

Jacó já tinha acumulado abundância de posses terrenas. O que mais poderia querer? Foi uma noite escura para Jacó quando descobriu que havia passado a vida perseguindo posses e resistindo a Deus. Agora busca caráter piedoso e riqueza espiritual. Sua vitória veio pela rendição, e saiu mancando como um aleijado com uma coroa. O Senhor não pode abençoar plenamente um homem até que tenha primeiro vencido seus poderes de razão.

…Fado Ruim

Como também os principais sacerdotes e nossos magistrados o entregaram para ser condenado à morte, e o crucificaram –Lucas 24:20. Deus é especialista em transformar graves dilemas em vitórias monumentais. Ainda assim, o homem olha ao seu redor e amaldiçoa as trevas que o cercam. Embora possa haver uma saraivada de bem retribuindo-lhes, …a manhã para eles é como a sombra da morte… –Jó 24:17. Dar ênfase indevida ao mal que nos cerca é zombar da divindade de Deus. Embora todos possamos nos arrepender às vezes de coisas que poderíamos ter feito ou dito de modo diferente, devemos invariavelmente deixar os resultados nas mãos de Deus. Jó experimentou tanto infortúnio quanto qualquer um. Tanto que ele abriu …a boca e amaldiçoou o seu dia. E Jó disse: Pereça o dia em que nasci, e a noite em que se disse: Foi concebido um homem. Seja esse dia tenebroso; não o estime o Senhor desde os céus, nem brilhe sobre ele a luz. Escureça-o a escuridão e a sombra da morte; habite sobre ele uma nuvem; assuste-o a obscuridade do dia. Quanto àquela noite, tome-a a escuridão… –Jó 3:1-6. Mas em algum lugar, antes que os eventos sombrios fossem retificados e levantados, a luz brilhou em sua alma, e ele levou a mão à boca e adorou.

…Agenda Pessoal

Mas nós esperávamos que fosse ele que havia de remir Israel… –Lucas 24:21. É natural tentar entender qualquer situação dada e esses dois haviam escolhido a equação correta. Sua tolice residia na presunção quanto aos meios pelos quais Cristo realizaria isto e no tipo de redenção que esperavam receber. Eles esperavam o dia em que sua nação seria exaltada sobre os romanos. Quando buscamos inadvertidamente nossa própria segurança, isso tende a levar a amarga decepção. Naamã pensou …certamente ele sairá a mim, e invocará o nome do SENHOR seu Deus, e sobre o lugar baterá com a mão, e sarará o leproso –2 Reis 5:11.

Abrão recebeu a promessa da terra de Canaã e pediu confirmação. Preparou então o sacrifício da aliança prescrito por Deus, mas o dia inteiro passou, e Deus nada fez com eles. E sucedeu que, quando o sol se punha, caiu sobre Abrão um sono profundo; e eis que uma grande e terrível escuridão caiu sobre ele. –Gênesis 15:12.

Enquanto Abrão esperava em Deus para receber sua oferta, continuou a espantar as aves de rapina. Mas, à medida que o dia chegava ao fim, começou a sentir-se abandonado por Deus e a noite escura passou a assentar-se sobre sua alma. É preciso uma experiência de meia-noite para que as coisas fiquem escuras o suficiente para vermos as estrelas e quietas o bastante para ouvirmos Sua voz. Mas nós tínhamos já em nós o sentenciamento para a morte, para não confiarmos em nós mesmos, mas em Deus que ressuscita os mortos –2 Coríntios 1:9.

…Impaciência

…E além de tudo isto, é hoje o terceiro dia que estas coisas se fizeram –Lucas 24:21. Muitos de nós são disciplinados o suficiente para aguentar por uma estação. É quando nossa esperança é demorada (ver Provérbios 13:12) que nossos corações adoecem e enfraquecem. Três dias pareceram muito tempo para esses dois. Mas três dias, semanas, meses, anos, ou mesmo décadas estão todos dentro do relógio de Deus. Até quando, SENHOR, te esquecerás de mim para sempre? até quando esconderás de mim o teu rosto? –Salmo 13:1.

José suportou pacientemente o maltrato de seus irmãos e de Potifar, mas a masmorra ficou longa, e ele rogou ao copeiro que se lembrasse dele quando fosse restituído ao seu posto. Mas se passaram dois anos inteiros (Gênesis 41:1) até que Faraó sonhasse e José fosse finalmente chamado. Mas não foi tanto culpa do copeiro quanto da vontade de Deus, que havia chamado José para ser …posto em cadeias: até que viesse a sua palavra; a palavra do SENHOR o viu. –Salmo 105:18-19. Não há caminho mais eficaz para nos ensinar paciência do que a disciplina das trevas, da qual poucos santos estão isentos.

…Autocomiseração

E também algumas mulheres dentre nós nos fizeram espantar, as quais, estando de manhã cedo no sepulcro, não achando o seu corpo, vieram dizendo que também haviam visto visão de anjos, os quais disseram que ele vive –Lucas 24:22-23. Ninguém gosta de ficar de fora. De fato, a psicologia descobriu um novo transtorno — FOMO (fear of missing out, medo de perder algo). A notícia trazida pelas mulheres era boa e uma virada de eventos espantosa, ainda assim não trouxe alegria aos outros porque não aconteceu com eles. Boas novas raramente penetram numa pessoa imersa em autocomiseração, e Elias foi uma dessas. Sua noite escura chegou na esteira de uma vitória de tirar o fôlego no monte Carmelo contra os profetas de Baal. Mas na escuridão de seus próprios sentimentos …pediu pela própria morte e disse: Basta! tira-me agora a minha vida, pois não sou melhor do que meus pais –1 Reis 19:4.

…Sentimentos de Fracasso

E alguns dos que estavam conosco foram ao sepulcro, e acharam assim como as mulheres disseram; porém não o viram –Lucas 24:24. É fácil pensar: “Funcionou para eles, mas não está funcionando para mim.” Embora esforços sem sucesso possam nos desencorajar, não é necessariamente um fracasso da nossa parte. João Batista havia chamado fielmente o povo ao arrependimento, batizou Cristo e testemunhou a voz trovejante do céu. Anunciou com precisão o Messias vindouro e apontou seus discípulos para …o Cordeiro de Deus, que tira o pecado do mundo –João 1:29. Esse ministério lhe rendeu um lugar seguro numa cela escura de prisão. Estava bem acostumado à falta de conforto e a uma dieta magra, mas foi o sentimento de abandono total por parte de Deus que o trouxe a dúvidas sombrias. E João, chamando dois de seus discípulos, enviou-os a Jesus, dizendo: És tu aquele que havia de vir, ou esperamos outro? –Lucas 7:19.

“Estive enganado?” Na escuridão, ele começou a experimentar a vida no lombo inclinado de um ponto de interrogação. John Bunyan descreve isso como o pântano do desespero. Pode parecer o Dia D para o cristão, mas ênfase indevida em nossos esforços malsucedidos não promove qualquer ressurreição.

Conclusão

Nem toda escuridão espiritual é completamente evitável. Nem toda experiência espiritual é tempo de verdadeira bênção, nem todo lugar. Há tempos de perseguição e provação que são destinados a trazer os santos ao balanço da alma que somente as noites escuras podem ministrar. O próprio Jesus foi tentado de modo semelhante a nós, quando na escuridão predominante da nona hora na cruz, Sua voz ressoou …com grande voz, dizendo: Eli, Eli, lama sabactâni? isto é: Deus meu, Deus meu, por que me desamparaste? –Mateus 27:46.

A estrada para Emaús testemunha o fato de que uma existência vibrante de fé não garante a ausência de depressão espiritual. É uma história sobre pessoas reais com fé real enfrentando provações reais. É útil para nos ensinar que até prazeres espirituais não devem ser segurados com demasiada firmeza. Nossas visões confiantes para o futuro, tanto imediato quanto a longo prazo, devem ser imersas nos fogos da humildade. A noite escura é o lugar onde tal autoengano morre, e nasce um conhecimento íntimo de Deus. Transforma-nos de amar a Deus pelas bênçãos que Ele nos dá, para amar a Deus por nosso relacionamento com Ele e a comunhão que se segue.

O companheiro de viagem de Cleopas nunca foi mencionado. Alguns pensam que era sua esposa. Outros afirmam que era Lucas. Mas sua identidade foi omitida, talvez para que estejamos mais inclinados a preencher a vaga com nosso próprio nome. Sete milhas de Jerusalém tropeçamos na dura realidade de quem o Salvador realmente é e que a salvação é mais do que um carimbo de borracha marcando Sua posse. As escamas caem de nossos olhos e a noite escura da alma dá lugar ao brilho da luz do meio-dia da presença de Deus. É então que fazemos nossa alegre corrida de volta à cidade da paz apenas para ser novamente incompreendidos. E foram e deram a notícia ao restante; e não creram neles –Marcos 16:13.

E assim, até me pergunto sobre a utilidade de escrever tais pensamentos. Não é um encontro que possa ser fabricado e intelectualmente compreendido. É uma convocação altamente pessoal com Deus e feita sob medida para cada indivíduo. Mas talvez nós, em nossa geração rasa, possamos ser encorajados a estender a mão e abraçar a escuridão em vez de encará‑la com aversão e resistência. E ali, na escuridão ameaçadora da noite, aprender a abraçar o Salvador da luz.

Longo tempo meu espírito aprisionado jaz,
Firmemente acorrentado no pecado e na noite da natureza.
Teu olhar difundiu um raio vivificante,
Acordei; a masmorra flamejou com luz.
Minhas correntes caíram. Meu coração ficou livre.
Levantei-me, saí e te segui.

- Charles Wesley
